articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of the Accuracy of NDTs in Determining Concrete Strength
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: In evaluating the effectiveness of various nondestructive tests (NDTs), the results obtained through ultrasonic pulse velocity and the Schmidt hammer were compared on concrete cylinders, manufactured with a 4000 psi mix, evaluated at 7 and 28 days. Correlation equations were developed to relate the results of these NDTs with the actual concrete strength, obtaining $R^{2}$ values ranging from $17.8 \%$ to $52.7 \%$. The results indicated that the Schmidt hammer showed a stronger correlation with compressive strength, reaching a maximum $R^{2}$ of $52.7 \%$, while the ultrasonic pulse velocity showed a maximum $R^{2}$ of $34.9 \%$. Additionally, moisture was found to significantly influence the results of both tests, affecting both pulse velocity and rebound number. These equations provide useful tools for engineers, allowing them to assess concrete strength more accurately without the need for sample extraction, thus optimizing inspection and maintenance processes for structures.

articleTitle: Analysis of information consumption and the impact of the UTP institutional repository on the dissemination of academic knowledge
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Today’s universities are undergoing constant change, driven by the knowledge society and Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs), which facilitate access to information. In this context, open access has become an essential tool for scientific dissemination, enabling the preservation and visibility of academic output through institutional repositories (IR). The study focuses on RIDDA2, the institutional repository of the Technological University of Panama (UTP), which houses 3,491 documents. However, the survey revealed that only $50 \%$ of respondents were aware of the repository’s existence, and of these, only $31 \%$ had uploaded documents. Although repositories are less utilized compared to other information sources like academic social networks, those who use them find valuable materials. The importance of institutional repositories for academic visibility is highlighted, but there is also a need to increase their promotion within the university community to enhance both their usage and the volume of content deposited. This boost is crucial for strengthening the visibility and impact of the university’s scientific output..

articleTitle: Propuesta del uso del Sistema de Identificación Automática y Machine Learning para el análisis de los buques posicionados en el Canal de Panamá
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: This paper proposes the use of the Automatic Identification System and Machine Learning to analyze the activities and operational conditions of vessels positioned on the Atlantic and Pacific sides of the Panama Canal. In this stage of the study, the objective was to analyze by means of Exploratory Data Analysis, the data from the Automatic Identification System, to identify the activities, operational conditions and positioning of vessels in both slopes. The preliminary analysis showed that 55‥ of the data corresponds to hazardous cargo and container vessels, the average speed of the vessels in the underway state using the engine is 1.10 knots. This suggests that vessels are possibly moving between locks or performing transit maneuvers. Whereas, for the moored and anchored navigation states, the average speeds are 0.43 and 0.42 knots respectively, suggesting that the vessels are stopped, either moored or anchored, waiting to initiate transit. Summarizing, through the Automatic Identification System, the preliminary characteristics and behavioral patterns of the ships are known, serving as a starting point for the selection of the Machine Learning algorithm that will lead to a more detailed study to know the levels and trend of emissions from ships.

articleTitle: Trends in the evaluation of energy efficiency and thermal comfort in buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: This article summarizes a bibliometric review aimed at analyzing the behavior of contributions related to the evaluation of energy efficiency and thermal comfort in buildings (EEETCB). A review of 231 papers indexed in SCOPUS between 2004 and 2024 was carried out. The study showed that “Thermal Comfort”, “Energy Saving”, “Energy Efficiency” were the most used keywords in the papers, while words such as “HVAC”, “Indoor Air Quality”, “Energy Consumption and Conservation” are strongly interconnected. The analysis revealed that studies on EEETCB have tended to grow and that well-known journals in the fields of energy, building and environment have produced numerous publications on the subject.

articleTitle: Lean Supply Chain Management and agri-food 4.0 model: The case of peruvian coffee supply chain
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The agri-food supply chain faces the challenge of increasing its flow of raw materials by 70% to satisfy demand by 2050. The supply chain of the coffee industry presents deficiencies in its activities and processes, and as it is the second most marketed in the world, it is of great importance to analyze the performance of your supply chain in the phases it goes through. This study seeks to analyze the processes directly affecting the operational performance of coffee farms. We integrate Lean Supply Chain Management with Industry 4.0 tools and improve the operating performance by 17%. Finally, significant improvements have been demonstrated in the reduction of waste and the optimization of the agri-food supply chain.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Angle Type Shear Connector in Steel Beam with Deck Slab
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: As is known in the various international codes, there is no expression for calculating the shear-resistant capacity of angle-type connectors that can be used in steel and concrete composite beams. Based on this and their potential use in building construction in Ecuador due to their low cost, a study is being conducted at the Housing Research Center of the National Polytechnic School in Quito, Ecuador, with the objective of obtaining an expression for this calculation. The research presented here aims to analyze the shear resistance of 4 mm thick angle profiles welded vertically in two different positions: at 45 degrees and at 90 degrees. Ten specimens were prepared, with five containing connectors for each orientation, utilizing concrete with a compressive strength of 31 MPa obtained from laboratory tests. The specimens underwent push-out tests, yielding load-slip data that were then subjected to statistical analysis. The analysis included parameters such as resistance, ductility, energy dissipation, and failure modes. It was concluded that the predominant failure mode in all specimens was the fractionation of concrete above the crest of the deck and across its entire width. Regarding ductility, both positions exhibited similar behavior, while those positioned at 90 degrees demonstrated greater resistance compared to those at 45 degrees.

articleTitle: Application of the RUSLE Method in the Development of Erosion Susceptibility Maps: A Case Study of a Micro-Watershed in Tierras Altas, Chiriquí.
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: This work addresses the application of the RUSLE (Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation) method for creating erosion susceptibility maps in a micro-watershed located in the Tierras Altas region, Chiriquí. The study area focuses on the district of Cerro Punta, an agricultural area characterized by steep slopes. The study aims to delineate the likelihood of soil erosion through susceptibility mapping using the RUSLE methodology, which requires the analysis of freely accessible data such as geomorphology, soil classification, land use, and precipitation to estimate the erosion potential of the area. The results show an erosive potential in the study area with values ranging from 0 to 7975 (t ha-1 year-1), with greater erosion observed in areas with agricultural activities, particularly horticulture. Erosion is distributed into five categories: low ($29.80 \%$), moderate ($19.21 \%$), high ($22.69 \%$), very high ($13.10 \%$), and severe ($15.20 \%$). This is due to the loss of vegetation cover in areas where agricultural practices are developed.

articleTitle: Interpretation of the changes in Forest Cover and Land Use driven by the evolution of Geotechnologies in the Republic of Panama (Period 1947-2021)
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The evolution of land use and land cover data has been a topic of interest for decades in decision-making and generation of national policies. Forest cover reports show estimates ranging between $5,245,000\mathrm{ha}(70\%$) for the year 1947 and ($68\%$) for the year 2021. The article shows the way in which the interpretation and analysis of aerial photographs and satellite images have been and They are essential data to identify and quantify vegetation cover through the evaluation of methodologies. In the 1940 s and 1970 s, forest coverage was obtained with aerial photographs and specialist knowledge of the territory. In the 1980 s, the first technological advance occurred, which began the era of medium-resolution satellite images, using visual interpretation techniques.. For the 90 s, these same images were used, but digital and automated processing was used to detect the spectral classes. In 2012, another technological leap was made, as a result of the use of images with higher spatial resolution, which allows for information on Forest Cover and Land Use, represented in 32 classes. In 2019, with a Panamanian professional specialized in satellite data processing, the Forest and Other Wooded Lands map was created, and by 2021 the use of high-resolution satellite image platforms is included as complementary data and data is generated. of Forest Cover and Land Use with 33 categories and the national capacity to produce this information every 5 years. The difference in the results derived from various data sources is evident, due to technological advances and the level of accessibility and availability of information.

articleTitle: Systematic review on the state of the art of sap flow studies in tropical forests
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Humid tropical forests, like all ecosystems, are a vital component of biological diversity and healthy ecosystems, offer a wide range of ecosystem services, from oxygen production and assimilation/sequestration of atmospheric carbon dioxide $\left(\mathrm{CO}_{2}\right)$, creation and stabilization of soils, watershed protection and supply of natural resources, including food, fiber, fuel, housing, and medicines, these ecosystems are very common in Panama. Due to this importance, the main objective of this research is to conduct a comprehensive literature review on the state of the art of sap flow in interurban tropical rainforests, in the last 10 years, for this purpose, keywords and search strategies were identified to obtain a selection 7 articles, from the years 2014 to 2024, from 474 articles that were previously examined.

articleTitle: Identification and Characterization of Stellar Bars: A Combined Approach of Isophote and Fourier Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: In this paper, we analyze the surface photometry of 42 spiral galaxies from the SDSS Data Release 3 in the r band, focusing on bar identification and characteristics in the local universe. Using ISOPHOTE and P2DFFT, we measure bar length and strength through elliptical isophote fitting and two-dimensional Fourier transforms. Surface photometry is crucial for studying galaxy morphology, revealing information about size, shape, and dynamics. Our study identified barred spiral galaxies with a frequency of 33% using Elliptical Isophote Analysis and 23% using Fourier Analysis. By combining both methods, we achieve a more comprehensive assessment, allowing for the precise measurement of bar length and strength. These methods are complementary and particularly effective for galaxies with large bulges and prominent spiral arms. Our ongoing research aims to extend this approach with automated applications to a larger sample of galaxies.

articleTitle: Analysis of Parameters for Additive Manufacturing from Recycled HDPE Material
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: High-density polyethelene (HDPE) is one of the most widely used plastics due to its mechanical properties and high recyclability. However, its recycling rates remain low, leading to significant environmental issues. This research focuses on recycling HDPE to manufacture filaments used in 3D printing, thereby promoting the circular economy. The study details the materials, equipment, and extrusion process used for producing the recycled filament, as well as its application in 3D printing. The results demonstrate that the recycled HDPE filament maintains good mechanical properties and is feasible for use in additive manufacturing. However, issues such as adhesion problems and dimensional stability have been identified, requiring further optimization to enhance its recycling applications.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Literature Review on Constructed Wetlands: Design, Function, and Modeling Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: This article presents a comprehensive review of constructed wetlands (CWs), examining their design principles, operational functions, and modeling approaches within the context of wastewater treatment. Originating from the natural wetland systems utilized by ancient civilizations, CWs have evolved as effective, sustainable, and cost-efficient solutions for treating diverse wastewater types. The review methodology involved a thorough literature analysis using databases such as ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, and Scopus, with Mendeley Desktop© software employed for systematic archiving and organization of relevant studies. The overview section details the classification of CWs into surface and subsurface flow types, emphasizing their design considerations, including hydraulic load, pollutant removal mechanisms, and the role of vegetation. Advances in CWs modeling are discussed, highlighting the shift from simplistic empirical models to more complex mechanistic and AI-driven approaches that better capture the intricacies of CWs processes. Despite significant progress, challenges remain, particularly in integrating holistic models and addressing data limitations. The review concludes that ongoing innovation and interdisciplinary research are essential for optimizing CW performance and enhancing their role in sustainable water management. This synthesis of current knowledge aims to inform future research directions and improve the practical application of CWs in various environmental and operational contexts.

articleTitle: Analysis of Fuzzing Techniques to Discover Vulnerabilities in the Firmware of Internet of Things Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Implementing fuzzing to discover vulnerabilities in IoT devices is a field that is under active research. These devices are launched to market with many vulnerabilities, and fuzzing provides a way to detect them in an effective and efficient way. This research aims to identify the innovative techniques presented by these fuzzing methods. Current studies have focused on gray box fuzzers, since most are based on proven methods and tools. One of its disadvantages is that it relies on active access to the firmware binaries to emulate the device on a fuzzer control system. This access is not always possible due to commercial or technical restrictions. In these cases, black box fuzzers provide a functional alternative where access to these binaries is not available.

articleTitle: Open-Source Integration Environment for Industrial Robot Arm NACHI MZ04 with ROS
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: This research proposes an alternative strategy for the development of an open-source robot integration environment capable of providing an open communication, motion control and visualization interface for the NACHI MZ04 industrial robot. This environment is intended for conducting academic studies and industrial integration testing and evaluation. The integration environment allows modernization of the robotic system through the Robot Operating System (ROS) framework, and TCP/IP protocol. Additionally, a people detection system was integrated to avoid collisions between the industrial robot and users, through the use of IP cameras and the YOLOV8 image processing algorithm. Likewise, a motion control interface and a low-level controller were created for planning trajectories, controlling gripper opening/closing, among other tasks. As a complement, a graphical user interface (GUI) was implemented in which the main data of the integration environment is displayed, using the Custom Tkinter library.

articleTitle: Water consumption and CO2 emissions of concrete production in Panama as a function of the mix design
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: This study shows variability in water consumption and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions per cubic meter for different concrete mix designs, using data from Panama. Eight mix designs with different compressive strengths, were evaluated as a pilot study. The analysis considered processes within the production plant, transportation to the construction site, and the production of aggregates and cement. Primary data on water and energy consumption were obtained directly from local producers, and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions were calculated using the "Reduce Your Carbon Footprint" tool. The study found variability in water consumption and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions according to the compressive strength of the concrete. In the low consumption scenario, water consumption ranged from 400 to $600 \mathrm{~L} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$, while in the high consumption scenario, it ranged from 1100 to $1300 \mathrm{~L} / \mathrm{m}^{3} . \mathrm{CO}_{2}$ emissions varied between 100 and $300 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~CO}_{2} \mathrm{~eq} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$ in the low consumption scenario, and between 200 and $500 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~CO}_{2} \mathrm{eq} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$ in the high consumption scenario. These results emphasize the need for geographically contextualized studies of consumption and emissions. Although this study presents data from only eight mix designs, it highlights the importance of creating a database that allows for studying variability and identifying optimal ranges of consumption and emissions for concrete production in Panama, to reduce resource consumption, ecological footprint, and increase efficiency.

articleTitle: Variación espacial en la estación seca de las características fisicoquímicas del agua marino-costera en Bahia Damas, Parque Nacional Coiba, Panamá
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: This study measured physicochemical parameters in the marine waters of the euphotic zone at Coiba National Park in the Eastern Tropical Pacific of Panama during the 2023 dry season. Three sampling sites were established in Damas Bay, where temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen, electrical conductivity, salinity, total dissolved solids, turbidity, density, and hydrostatic pressure were recorded in situ using a YSI ProDSS multi-parameter device at depths of $0,5,25$, and 50 meters. Additionally, concentrations of nitrates and phosphates were analyzed from collected water samples at the Technological University of Panama. Results indicated statistically significant negative correlations ($\mathrm{p}\lt0.001$) between depth and temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen, and electrical conductivity. Conversely, salinity, total dissolved solids, density, hydrostatic pressure, and nutrient concentrations showed statistically significant positive correlations with depth ($\mathbf{p} \lt 0.001$). Phosphate levels ranged from 0.11 to $1.50 \mu \mathrm{M}$, with an average of $0.17 \mu \mathrm{M}$ at 25 meters, aligning with reported values. Nitrate concentrations averaged $0.33 \mu \mathrm{M}$ up to 25 meters, lower than the reported $0.6 \mu \mathrm{M}$ for Coiba’s dry season. These findings underscore the influence of depth, proximity to the coast, and oceanographic conditions on nutrient concentrations, highlighting the necessity for ongoing research to detect seasonal and annual variations. This research was supported by the SENACYT - CEMCIT-AIP PFID-FID-2021-170 macro project.

articleTitle: Automating the Transformation of Tidy Data on Morbidity Causes from INEC with R
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: In today’s digital age, Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) have revolutionized the availability of accurate and timely data, benefiting governments, productive sectors, and academia. Open government data promotes transparent, participatory, and efficient societies. In Panama, this effort is led by the National Authority for Transparency and Access to Information and the National Institute of Statistics and Census (INEC). Although INEC has been publishing extensive data since 2009, its format does not always meet FAIR standards nor is it organized, making its efficient use challenging. To address this challenge, an algorithm in R was developed to transform INEC morbidity data, drastically reducing transformation time. Compared to manual methods using Excel, the algorithm showed a significant reduction in transformation time: from 30.37 minutes to just 8.59 seconds per document.

articleTitle: Track of coastal zones through citizen science programs
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Due to climate change and the increase of anthropogenic activities in coastal areas, the vulnerability of coastal communities has increased, presenting problems such as coastal erosion. The purpose of this research is to identify coastal sites in the Pacific coast of Panama that are relevant for citizen science programs focused on coastline monitoring. The first list focused on two criteria, accessibility and climatic background, e.g. flood zones due to climate change. From this, and through a multi-criteria analysis, 10 pre-selected sites were obtained. As a result, a matrix of sites vs. criteria was elaborated and these were marked on maps.

articleTitle: Relationship Between Soil Texture and Infiltration Rate in the Guararé River Sub-basin
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The Guararé River sub-basin is in the province of Los Santos, Azuero Region, known for being part of the dry arc of Panama due to the low amount of rainfall recorded in the area, which averages 1,500 mm/year. In addition, it is the only region in the country that faces a water deficit situation; this region frequently reports drought periods of up to seven months. Therefore, the objective of this research was to determine the soil texture and estimate the infiltration rate of the sub-basin. The methodology consisted of taking soil samples at 59 points in the study area to determine their texture with the help of different ASTM Standards. In addition to estimating the infiltration rate at each point, using a Mini Disk infiltration meter. The results were analyzed with computer tools such as Excel MACROS, RStudio and ArcGIS Pro. The results were congruent with respect to the relationship between soil texture vs. infiltration rate. Identifying key areas for water conservation in the basin.

articleTitle: Caracterización del entorno de los puentes peatonales y su distribución espacial en Panamá
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: La investigación realizada se centra en la caracterización del entorno de los puentes peatonales y su distribución espacial en Panamá, con el objetivo de analizar la importancia que tienen los mismos dentro de la movilidad urbana y la seguridad vial en el país. La metodología implementada se divide en tres fases principales. Primero, se utilizó ArcGIS Pro para geolocalizar los puentes peatonales a nivel nacional, estimando la distancia recorrida por los peatones al cruzar los puentes y la distancia aproximada de las aceras adyacentes, proporcionando una base sólida para el análisis posterior. Se empleó Google Maps con Street View para describir los entornos adyacentes, evaluando factores como la accesibilidad, el estado de mantenimiento, la seguridad, la iluminación, la señalización y la presencia de mobiliario urbano, obteniendo una comprensión integral del contexto en el que se encuentran los puentes. Finalmente, se evaluaron los resultados obtenidos para generar recomendaciones basadas en evidencias, identificando patrones y áreas de mejora que informan la planificación y el mantenimiento de los puentes peatonales. La importancia de esta investigación radica en su capacidad para proporcionar una visión detallada y basada en datos de la situación actual de los puentes peatonales en Panamá. Este estudio no solo destaca la necesidad de mejorar la infraestructura existente, sino que también identifica oportunidades para la implementación de nuevas estructuras que aumenten la seguridad y eficiencia del tránsito peatonal.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal variation of hydrological and bacteriological conditions in the estuary of Río Salado-Bahía de Chame
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: This study focuses on the evaluation of water quality in the mangrove estuary of the Salado River in Chame Bay, Panama, through the analysis of physicochemical and biological parameters. Quarterly samplings were carried out at four stations along the estuary: Upper Estuary, Middle Estuary, Lower Estuary and Chame Bay, during the dry and rainy seasons, to determine the spatiotemporal variations. The results showed significant differences between the two seasons. In the rainy season, higher levels of pH and total coliforms were recorded, suggesting an increase in the entrainment of sediments and waste. In the dry season, higher concentrations of nitrates and phosphates were observed, attributed to the phenomenon of coastal upwelling, where deep, nutrient-rich waters rise to the surface. Levels of E. coli, an indicator of fecal contamination, remained generally low but increased markedly in the upper estuary during the dry season, possibly due to the presence of mammals in the area and the lack of runoff. This study highlights the importance of considering seasonal variations and specific ecological dynamics of the estuary for its sustainable management. These results are crucial for the development of conservation and management strategies for mangrove ecosystems in the region, providing valuable data that can help establish effective environmental management policies. Continuous monitoring and a comprehensive approach that considers both natural influences and human activities are necessary to preserve these vital ecosystems..

articleTitle: Trabajo infantil en Panamá (2014 y 2016)
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: In Panama there are more than 23 thousand minors who are victims of child labor according to figures from the National Institute of Statistics and Census (INEC). This research analyzes the data obtained from the Child Labor Survey conducted during the years 2014 and 2016, to compare them and determine the characteristics in which their participation occurs. In addition, the study provides fundamental statistical models and calculations to estimate the relationships between variables that help to monitor and evaluate the programs carried out by the different social agents, resulting in a decrease in child labor in the Republic of Panama between 2014 and 2016 in all age ranges studied (from 5 to 17 years old), concluding that Panama is one of the countries in Latin America and the Caribbean that most progress has been made in the process of eradicating child labor.

articleTitle: Sustained attention in children with ASD: A comparative analysis between traditional intervention and the use of the MyRoT robotic tree
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: We investigated the effectiveness of the intervention through the MyRoT robot tree as a didactic support on the development of sustained attention in children with ASD. A mixed approach study was carried out with 14 IPHE students diagnosed with ASD aged 5 to 12 years, they were divided into: Group A (control), face-toface intervention and Group B, remote intervention through MyRoT. We analyze the number of correct answers and the level of sustained attention by measuring the focusing time, using the parameter established in the RETAS document, proposed by us. We used a significance level of 0.05 for Student’s T tests (focusing time and number of correct answers) and Pearson classification. By not observing significant differences in focusing time and correctness, we conclude that the intervention modality does not influence the development of sustained attention. We did not find an estimate between focusing time and successes. However, both groups presented equality in the amount of achievement, according to the ABA model, and reached adequate levels of sustained attention according to RETAS, supporting the usefulness of MyRoT for remote interventions. Furthermore, students in group B demonstrated spontaneous interactions towards MyRoT, suggesting a potential to improve social skills, spontaneous language, communicative intention and emotion recognition in children with ASD.

articleTitle: Optical properties of bilayer systems of gold and silver
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The optical properties of metallic materials change abruptly when at least one of their dimensions is reduced to the nanometric scale. Metallic nanostructures exhibit the phenomenon of surface plasmon resonance, which corresponds to the coherent and collective oscillation of free electrons under the excitation of electromagnetic radiation. In thin films nanostructures, surface plasmons are propagative waves along the metal-dielectric interface and their resonance frequency depends on the type of metal and the surrounding dielectric. One of the most studied plasmonic systems is nanometric thin films of gold and silver due to their noble properties, which is a great advantage for sensor applications. This work aims to prepare more complex systems (bilayers) of gold on silver and silver on gold to understand how the plasmonic response is enhanced or affected depending on the thickness ratio and how it differs from traditional single-metal systems. Experimental measurements were performed by measuring reflectance as a function of the incidence angle using the Kretschmann configuration and numerical simulations were performed to interpret the data using the Pyllama Python library based on the transfer matrix method. The main results show that for the gold-on-silver (Au/Ag) system the best plasmonic response is obtained for the Au-34nm/Ag-24nm sample and for the silver-on-gold (Ag/Au) system the best response is obtained for the Ag-38nm/Au-23nm sample.

articleTitle: Low Cost Optical Maskless Photolithography Patterning for Pt/Ti Micro-Electrodes for Microelectromechanical Systems Using a Microlight 3D System
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The research described in this article focused on developing a process to produce microelectrodes $20 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ long/ $10 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ wide ($\lt {5 0} \mu \mathrm{m}$ sideway dimension, which is the current limit for metal structures produced by lift-off patterning using a microlight 3D system), using maskless photolithography equipment (SmartPrint UV Microlight 3D) for exposing a thin layer of nlof 2020 negative photoresist sensitive to i-line. The sacrificial nlof 2020 layer used is $\sim 2 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ thick, estimated from the provider technical data sheet. First, a rectangular cantilever was patterned on the substrate. The patterning process revealed that increasing the intensity of the UV light enables to increase the resolution to produce smaller structures on the photoresist layer, which is not regularly done by contact mask photolithography. UV light exposure time, and prebaking and post-baking time were also varied to optimize the definition of the electrode structures. Finally, the process was integrated on top of an ultrananocrystalline diamond (UNCD)-based microcantilever for testing the process as second step in the development of UNCD-based microcantilevers.

articleTitle: Implementación De Un Modelo De Simulación En SUMO Para Optimizar La Gestión Del Tráfico Terrestre En La Terminal Portuaria De Balboa
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: La terminal portuaria de Balboa, un nodo crucial en la red de transporte marítimo de América Central enfrenta desafíos significativos en la gestión del tráfico terrestre que afectan su eficiencia operativa. Este estudio utiliza el software de simulación SUMO (Simulation of Urban MObility) para evaluar tres propuestas de mejora: kioscos autogestionados, programación de citas, y zonas de flujo rápido. El objetivo es identificar cuál de estas soluciones optimiza los tiempos de espera en los procesos de importación, exportación y trasiego. Las simulaciones iterativas revelarán el impacto de cada propuesta, proporcionando una visión integral para enfrentar los desafíos actuales y futuros de la terminal. El análisis busca no solo mejorar la eficiencia operativa, sino también incrementar la competitividad del Puerto de Balboa a nivel regional.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Influence of Welding Conditions on the Angular Deformation and Residual Stresses in Thick Plate using FEM
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Welding conditions are a set of parameters such as amperage, voltage, welding speed, and efficiency, which significantly influence the heat input during the process. When joining steel pieces through welding, thermal loads are induced, resulting in imperfections like angular deformation and residual stresses. If not properly controlled, these imperfections can compromise the quality, integrity, and durability of structures. Consequently, numerous studies have investigated the influence of heat input on welding defects in various types of joints, commonly butt, and T joints, through the control of welding parameters. This study employs a Thermo-Elasto-Plastic Analysis (TEPA) using the Finite Element Method (FEM) to examine the impact of welding conditions on T-joints of thick S355J2 steel plates, widely used as stiffeners. The Gas Metal Arc Welding (GMAW) process is considered to recommend an optimal range of welding conditions to minimize angular deformation and residual stresses.

articleTitle: Education 4.0 and implementation of ICT at the high school level: case study in Santiago de Veraguas
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The new technological era has given rise to the concept of Education 4.0, which seeks to implement strategies for the use of ICT in the teaching-learning process, which promotes the training of competitive professionals who can respond to current trends and changes in the industry. Panama must solve inequities in terms of access and mastery of technological tools in secondary education. Placing a magnifying glass on the district of Santiago de Veraguas, a study was conducted on the use of technological tools at the high school level. Results indicate that currently its use is occasional, and the hardware and software catalog is basic; therefore, the need to promote strategies to increase the use of these instruments and ensure the success of students when advancing towards higher education is evident.

articleTitle: Determination of a Sustainability Index from Environmental Factor Assessments Applied to Port Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The Index of Sustainability of Port Operations (ISOP) assesses and improves port sustainability through environmental indicators. Its objective is to measure the efficiency of environmental management in ports, identifying and mitigating negative impacts. A methodology is used to collect and analyze data based on pressure, status and response indicators, evaluated quantitatively and qualitatively. The result is a numerical value that reflects the level of sustainability of a facility, facilitating the identification of areas for improvement and decision-making. The research reveals that the ISOP improves port practices and promotes technologies that reduce the environmental footprint, in addition to highlighting the need for training and adequate infrastructure. It is recommended to continue improving this index and promote its adoption globally to encourage more responsible and sustainable practices in the sector.

articleTitle: Analysis of Deep Foundations Subject to Lateral Loads in Stratified Soils Using the Finite Difference Method
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The use of piles for the construction of structures is a common practice to provide greater support. The issues that typically arise when employing this type of deep foundations stem from the soil-structure interaction. In this paper, the soil-structure interaction of piles installed in stratified soils is analyzed using the finite difference method and existing p-y curve methods available in the literature. To perform this analysis, electronic spreadsheets were developed to simulate the behavior of piles under lateral loads. Specifically, the p-y curve methods for piles installed in sand [1], clay [2], and stratified soils [3] were utilized. The results obtained from the developed spreadsheets were validated by comparing them with field tests found in the literature and the LPile software. Finally, a key conclusion is that the developed spreadsheets are useful in the pre-design phase of piles under lateral loads because the results obtained from the spreadsheets are shown to be conservative compared to the results obtained from engineering software and tests found in the literature.

articleTitle: Sociotechnical debt in Software projects: measuring sociotechnical factors impacting requirements elicitation
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Requirements elicitation is a fundamental stage in software development because it sets the conceptual basis for constructing software that seeks to satisfy the needs of clients and end users. However, during this stage, requirements elicitation teams face obstacles that can affect the accuracy and clear understanding of the needs and requirements specifications. Those obstacles are factors that indicate the presence of sociotechnical debt. This research aims to identify factors related to sociotechnical debt during requirements elicitation. Through literature analysis, we identified obstacles linked to sociotechnical debt in requirements elicitation. We developed EDReqAnalysis, a software prototype that automates the identification of sociotechnical obstacles in Jira (software to manage the development of software projects). The prototype detected three categories of obstacles: unaddressed user needs, requirement smells, and mismatched implementation.

articleTitle: Optimization of satellite biotelemetry data in seaturtles through outlier removal techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: This paper focuses on optimizing satellite telemetry data for green sea turtles (Chelonia mydas) by applying rigorous preprocessing and geospatial filtering techniques to eliminate outliers. The telemetry data, gathered from turtles equipped with SPOT-375B transmitters, included geographic positions and other relevant parameters. Initial preprocessing filtered out low-quality data, reducing the dataset by an average of 75.85%. A subsequent geospatial filter further removed data points recorded on land, accounting for an additional 5.25% reduction. These steps ensured that only accurate marine location data were used for analysis. The results demonstrate the critical importance of data cleaning and filtering in enhancing the accuracy and reliability of telemetry studies. This approach not only improves the precision of movement pattern analysis but also provides a robust framework for future studies in marine conservation. While effective, the study acknowledges the limitations of relying on coastline data resolution and suggests incorporating environmental variables in future research to further refine data interpretation.

articleTitle: Versatile hardware to Analyze the Performance of a Nonlinear Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: A sequential Lyapunov technique was developed to ensure the asymptotic stability of various mechanical systems. First, an Inverted Pendulum Cart, then a Hovercraft, and later a Quadrotor Subjected to a Variable Load. This study proposes a controller to be tested in a thermal system. While there is a growing trend towards developing low-cost control implementation equipment, successful performance offers many benefits, including easier adaptation and maintenance. To validate the designed controller, the hardware should accurately reflect the relationship between theory and what is expected in the real world. The designed experiments will allow the hardware to obtain experimental data that can correlate with models generated by the Temperature Lab. The control laboratory hardware is highly beneficial as it allows for modifying and improving experimental designs through the Temperature Lab, enabling analysis before incurring high costs. The experiments showed consistent performance considering the Extended Kalman Filter and Unscented Kalman Filter, leading to accurate results studied through numerical examples.

articleTitle: Phase Transitions in BiFeO3 through Thermoelectric Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The theoretical single crystal of BiFeO3 (BFO) with rhombohedral phase R3c was studied using Wu-Cohen (WC) and $\mathbf{W C}+\mathbf{U}$ exchange and correlation functionals. The representation of the core electrons was done through optimized Vanderbilt pseudopotentials (ONCV). The electronic band structure and density of states (DOS) were determined after the atoms of the system were relaxed. The results show a valence band densely populated compared to the conduction band, and whose band gap is close to 2.33 eV. Calculations of the thermoelectric parameters as a function of temperature are presented and indicate the existence of two-phase transitions in the range from 50 to 800 K, which are discussed.

articleTitle: Applying fuzzy-AHP in agile supply chain management: A study in a Peruvian paint company
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: This document analyzes and searches for the background and fuzzy-AHP implementation results in supply chains where agile management was implemented in a Peruvian painting company. Supply chain agility is important. It permits production according to clients’ needs and responds quickly to changes in demand and delivery time. F-AHP implementation allows greater management agility of the supply chain, by analyzing the actors and selecting best factors for agile supply chain so that the company can run smoothly. The factors evaluated are the suppliers, the manufacturing area and the distributors. After the application of fuzzy-AHP in this work, first supplier, second distributor and the first manufacturer have higher scores compared to the others, therefore the process chooses them since these are the best options in order to obtain an agile supply chain management. Finally, this document demonstrates the approach, seeks to follow through with the F-AHP method and provides the best selection.

articleTitle: Towards Sustainable Forest Management – Advancing Autonomy Approach in Forestry Operations for the Forests of the Future
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Forestry is a vital economic sector in Austria, Europe, and many other regions worldwide. Modern machineries are extensively used for timber harvesting, selection, processing, and transportation across the diverse spectrum of forest management activities. These tasks often take place under challenging conditions, as forests are typically located in remote mountainous and valley areas. Currently, machines are powered by diesel engines and operated manually. This procedure has two major drawbacks: (1) diesel combustion produces significant emissions, and (2) manual operation endangers workers, leading to frequent severe accidents mainly due to human errors or misjudgments. Additionally, timber transportation depends on diesel-powered trucks, resulting in considerable CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions. To address these challenges, this paper presents measures aimed at achieving sustainable and automated timber harvesting and transportation processes. The ongoing research project focuses on two primary objectives: (1) reducing emissions through electrification and the use of local electric energy sources (e.g., hydroelectric power plants), and (2) developing autonomous forest transport systems, including loading-, unloading-, and transportation-processes.

articleTitle: LabSI-SAT: Low-cost CubeSat Nanosatellite Prototype Assembly Demonstration
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: This document is a report on the lessons learned during the construction of a low-cost nanosatellite prototype using commercially available components. It examines the system control models and sensors that can be utilized, as well as ways to enhance the reliability and availability of both hardware and software. The project was conducted using the space race achievements of other countries as a reference, with the goal of enabling other nations seeking to develop in this field to embark on their own space endeavors.

articleTitle: Percepción de riesgo y conocimiento popular sobre los caimanes y cocodrilos (Caiman crocodilus y Crocodylus acutus) en diez comunidades rivereñas de la Provincia de Darién, Panamá
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Two species of the order Crocodylia inhabit Panama: Caiman crocodilus fuscus (spectacled caiman) and Crocodylus acutus (American crocodile). Over the past 20 years, many of these reptile populations have shown considerable recovery. The increasing population density and coexistence with humans in shared habitats present a conservation challenge, as human-crocodile conflicts tend to escalate. In Panama, specifically in the province of Darién, there are no official records on human-crocodile encounters. The lack of studies on residents’ perception and knowledge regarding the ecology and biology of crocodiles and caimans impedes species conservation efforts. This research aims to qualitatively assess the level of knowledge and risk perception among inhabitants of ten communities in the Province of Darién, who regularly coexist with caimans and crocodiles. This was achieved through the on-site administration of a semistructured survey.During the dry season of 2023, 63 surveys were conducted among adult residents of both genders and various ethnicities in ten locations. All respondents correctly identified the two species of crocodylians based on morphology. Seventy-five percent were knowledgeable about the habitats of each species. Eighty-eight percent were aware of their dietary habits, although 18% incorrectly mentioned that they feed on humans. Only 40% knew the nesting habits of American crocodiles and caimans. Sixty-six percent admitted to consuming caiman or American crocodile meat. Eighty-nine percent engage in daily activities within crocodile habitats. Fifty-five percent reported personal experiences or heard of others encountering issues with American crocodiles or caimans, including five direct attacks on humans within the past five years.

articleTitle: Water quality of the Guararé and Perales river using aquatic macroinvertebrates as bioindicators
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The objective of this study was to know the quality of water through macroinvertebrate families in two sites for the Guararé River and one for the Perales River; The diversity and abundance of aquatic macroinvertebrates was determined. The sites sampled in the Guararé and Perales rivers were able to identify a total of four hundred and ninety-five individuals belonging to eleven orders of macroinvertebrates, of which nine belong to the class Insecta and two belong to the orders Molusca and Decápoda respectively. The orders with the greatest number of individuals recorded are: Ephemeropetera with two hundred individuals, Trichoptera with one hundred and sixty individuals and Diptera with thirty-five individuals. The results indicate that the water quality through the use of macroinvertebrates and applying the BMWP/Pan presented good quality values for the Cucula-Botoncillo point, while the Guararé1 Llano Abajo point indicates contaminated water quality, due to the disturbances present. in the study area, while the point of the Perales River, a tributary of the Guararé River, presented waters of regular quality. The diversity at the points of the Guararé River during sampling showed an average of $\mathbf{H}^{\prime}=\mathbf{2} .44$ for CuculaBotoncillo; $\mathbf{H}^{\prime}=\mathbf{2 . 0 1}$ for Guararel Llano Abajo and, $\mathbf{H}^{\prime}=1.87$ for the Perales River Shannon diversity ($\mathbf{H}^{\prime}$) presents a mean value for the sampled points, which indicates that they are influenced by anthropic factors; for the Simpson index (D) showed that at least two individuals captured at each of the collection points are of the same species.

articleTitle: Comparison of peaking factor of measured flow data from commercial users with empirical formulas
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Population growth and economic development are major drivers of increased global freshwater demand, with urban populations expected to rise from $54 \%$ to $66 \%$ by the century’s end. The Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) predicts a $55 \%$ increase in water demand since 2000, potentially putting over $\mathbf{4 0 \%}$ of the global population under severe water stress by 2050. Climate change and urbanization will exacerbate the challenge of ensuring urban water security. While expanding water infrastructure could help, geographical and financial constraints limit this approach. Alternatively, managing water demand through water-saving technologies, updated policies, and education can ensure a reliable supply and reduce costs. Residential water consumption in Panama has significant societal impact but is inefficiently tracked with traditional manual meter readings. Smart water meters provide a modern solution, offering continuous electronic readings. Despite the high initial costs, smart water meters improve water registration accuracy and management efficiency, enabling real-time usage monitoring and generating valuable datasets for water resource management. This study analyzed continuous water consumption data from a smart meter network at Universidad Tecnológica de Panamá’s cafeterias to calculate peaking factors and compare them with empirical formulas. Using a LoRaWAN framework, water flow data was collected, stored, and analyzed, with missing values imputed using Python. Significant discrepancies were found between peaking factors from empirical formulas and actual data, highlighting the need for extensive flow metering operations. The recorded water demand pattern matched the building’s daily activity, emphasizing the importance of smart meters for accurate water consumption estimation and improved management.

articleTitle: Performance study of basalt fiber polymer rebar (BFRP) compared to carbon steel bars.
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Basalt fiber polymer rebars represent a viable alternative for use in structures located in aggressive environments due to their non-corrosive properties and high tensile strength. Tensile and bond tests, as well as flexural tests, were performed on reinforced concrete beams with both types of reinforcing bars to evaluate differences between crack widths, strains, and failure modes. These results will provide a basis for future research and applications in infrastructure in Panama.

articleTitle: Implementation of topographic techniques for monitoring coastal erosion
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Coastal erosion is the negative effect between the input and output of sediments in coastal areas. These alterations in the morphology of the coasts leave with them negative socioeconomic and ecosystem impacts. New topographic technologies allow monitoring coastal erosion at low cost and with large spatial coverage. This research seeks to compare topographic techniques with GNSS RTK and RPA PPK for monitoring coastal erosion. A comparison was made of beach profile measurements made with GNSS and RPA for one day (April 24, 2023) on the sandy beaches of Farallón, Coclé. A 450 m long transect was analyzed to determine: the difference in elevation of the averages of beach profiles and similarity (slope) of the profiles along the defined transect. The results showed an average elevation difference of 70 cm between both techniques and similar slopes of 0.10 for the average profiles constructed. It is concluded that the digital photogrammetry technique with RPA PPK can be used to conduct coastal erosion research in areas of difficult access, where humans do not have a greater reach. The beach profile survey technique using GNSS RTK can provide greater benefits when working on research with short-or medium-term monitoring. It is recommended that more studies of this type be carried out in coastal areas devoid of vegetation and infrastructure.

articleTitle: Agricultura regenerativa y manejo sostenible del suelo para la formación científica en institutos profesionales y técnicos de Panamá
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Regenerative agriculture is based upon an ecosystemic managementstrategy to improve food production, soil quality and sustainability for climate change adaptation. This case study was conducted in two Panamanian agricultural high schools (Gumercinda Páez and IPT México-Panamá). We established two field plots in each school with contrasting agricultural management practices: (i) conventional agriculture (soil tillage, synthetic fertilization, pesticides-herbicide application, continuous monoculture cropping) versus (ii) regenerative agriculture (minimum soil tillage, reduced fertilization, soil organic amendments, crop rotation, leguminous cover crops). Students and professors were responsible for plot management, tillage, planting, weed/pest control and harvest. A base line for soil properties was sampled before experimental plot planting. The soils in the plots were sampled about 6 and 14 months after planting for selected soil physical and chemical properties. In general, there were no significant differences in bulk density and penetration resistance between regenerative and conventional agriculture plots. The available P and K contents were higher in regenerative plots after 6 months, but the overall effect was reduced 14 months later. Soil reaction showed differences between plots at the beginning of the study, but the effect faded due to soil pH buffering capacity. Physical properties did not show significant differences between plots. Penetration resistance showed lower values with time after planting, in general. The professor and student body showed increased interest in soil science, regenerative agriculture practices and the scientific method overall. Limitations in infrastructure and government funding pose significant threats to the teaching-learning experience in Panama agricultural institutions of secondary education.

articleTitle: Energy Optimization in Software: A Comparative Analysis of Programming Languages and Code-Execution Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: This study investigates the differences in energy consumption between various programming languages, comparing those executed natively with those run on a Virtual Machine. The results challenge existing assumptions about the energy efficiency of software development practices. The findings reveal a positive correlation between the code execution strategy and resource consumption. Additionally, the study identifies key factors influencing the energy efficiency of applications beyond the choice of programming language. This research offers valuable insights for developers aiming to optimize energy consumption in their projects and prompts further questions regarding the future of development platforms and sustainable programming practices.

articleTitle: The threat of ocean acidification and its consequences for marine life and the coastal economy
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The study aims to assess the impact of ocean acidification on marine biodiversity and coastal economies dependent on these ecosystems. To this end, a review of the existing scientific literature was carried out, covering studies on ocean chemistry, marine biology and economic sciences. The methodology included a comparative analysis of data on ocean pH decline and its effects on calcifying organisms, as well as the modeling of possible future economic scenarios for coastal communities. The results reveal that acidification is causing a decrease in the ability of species such as corals and mollusks to form calcareous structures, leading to increased mortality and alterations in marine food webs. In addition, coastal communities, particularly those dependent on fishing and tourism, could face severe economic losses due to declines in biodiversity and the health of marine ecosystems. The study underscores the urgent need to implement mitigation and adaptation strategies to reduce the impacts of ocean acidification and protect both marine life and coastal economies.

articleTitle: Choosing a primary model to describe the growth curves of mountain microorganisms (Bioles)
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Mathematical models allow describing the dynamics of microbial populations under different environmental conditions. In this work, three models - Logistic, Gompertz and Baranyi-Roberts - were evaluated to characterize the growth of five beneficial bacteria present in a biological mountain soil. Model parameters were optimized using the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm. Statistical analyses, based on the root mean square error (RMSE), the coefficient of determination $\left(\mathrm{R}^2\right)$, the bias factor $\left(B_f\right)$) and the precision factor $A_f$), showed that the results show that the variability between strains suggests that the choice of the optimal model may depend on the specific characteristics of each strain, however, the Logistic model proved to be the most robust and consistent, offering the best fit to the experimental data in most strains.

articleTitle: Validation of different curing methods and their impact on the compressive strength of concrete
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The present research focuses on evaluating the impact of different curing methods on concrete compressive strength. The primary objective was to determine how variations in curing methods and temperature conditions affect the compressive strength of concrete. Four distinct curing methods were applied, each varying in initial and final curing conditions. Specimens were prepared and tested for compressive strength at 7 and 28 days, following ASTM C31 standard. The results indicated that curing methodology significantly impacts concrete strength. For instance, specimens exposed to higher temperatures showed higher strengths at early ages, while those left exposed to the elements exhibited lower strengths. These findings provide valuable insights for establishing effective curing practices tailored to Panama’s climatic conditions.

articleTitle: Extracción de ADN en Digestión Anaeróbica de Biosólidos: una herramienta versátil para optimizar la biometanización
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The metagenomic study of the microorganisms present in the anaerobic digestion of biosolids is important in a developing country like Panama. This techno-scientific information allows addressing the management problems of this waste, since it helps to know the microbial composition and thus find microorganisms that can positively or negatively affect those options of use, from energy, agriculture, etc. In this first stage of research, the method of digestivity tests is addressed, where using the Oxitop System, anaerobic digestion tests were developed at a temperature of 28°C obtaining results of biochemical methane potential of $\mathbf{3 1 3. 2 9}$ and $616.92 \mathrm{~mL} \mathrm{~CH}_4 /\mathrm{g} \mathrm{~SV}$. For later DNA extraction, a protocol was use by the manufacturer of a commercial kit specialized in environmental samples. Average purity concentrations ranged from 2.46 to $9.80 \mathrm{~ng} / \mu \mathrm{L}$ with absorbance measurements for $260 / 280$ ranging from 1.77 to 2.98. The values obtained from the DNA extractions with the commercial kit allow us to infer that the extracted DNA has the purity, quality, and integrity necessary for amplification and sequencing.

articleTitle: Nutrient distribution in a mangrove estuary in Bahia de Chame
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The spatiotemporal distribution of environmental variables and nutrients was evaluated along the Salado River estuary in the mangroves of Chame Bay. Four samplings were carried out, two in the rainy season and two in the dry season at three sites within the estuary and one external site with marine influence. Hydrological parameters were measured in situ and water samples were collected to determine nitrate $\left(\mathrm{NO}_{3}{ }^{-}\right)$, nitrite $\left(\mathrm{NO}_{2}-\right)$, ammonia $\left(\mathrm{NH}_{4}^{-}\right)$and phosphate $\left(\mathrm{PO}_{4}{ }^{3-}\right)$ in surface water. Gradients were detected in the spatial distribution of hydrological parameters and nutrients from the parts with greater fluvial influence to the external area of the estuary. Specifically, the variability between the salinity data set and the levels of pH and dissolved oxygen, ammonia and phosphate were not different between the internal sectors of the estuary and the site with marine influence, both in the rainy and dry seasons. The results presented are new evidence showing that the Salado River estuary is a system of great complexity, variability and dynamism.

articleTitle: 2D Electrical Resistivity Imaging for the Characterization of Soils near the Cerro Patacon Landfill, Panamá City
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: This research was developed with the 2D electrical resistivity tomography methodology to characterize the soils near the Cerro Patacón landfill; located at the southwest sector of the current waste deposit of Panama City. For the measurements, a total of 48 electrodes with a separation of $3 m$ were used. As a result, the range of electrical resistivity were obtained between 8.0 and 25.0 ohm.m. These values demonstrate that there are anomalies in the soil due to high electrical resistivity, which are associated to a rocky structure with low presence of discontinuities. On the other hand, zones with low electrical resistivity are associated with geological structures that have discontinuities.

articleTitle: Correlation of Electrical Resistivity in Concrete and Soils to Evaluate the Quality of Materials in Construction
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Electrical resistivity is a fundamental property for assessing the quality of construction materials, especially concrete and soil. In this study, we investigated the assessment between the electrical resistivity of these two materials, with the aim of establishing a reference framework for their joint application in defect detection and structural integrity assessment. Experimental tests were performed that included variations in chemical composition, moisture and texture, both in concrete and soil samples. The results indicate that there is a significant assessment between the electrical resistivity of concrete and soil under controlled conditions, suggesting that both materials can be jointly assessed to improve the accuracy in defect detection. This study provides a solid basis for the use of electrical resistivity as a non-destructive and efficient method in the quality assessment of construction materials, with practical implications in civil engineering and geotechnics.

articleTitle: Modeling Lean Manufacturing Using a Circularity Approach: An Empirical Study in a Peruvian Paint Company
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Delivering products is not just about getting them into the hands of the customer, but they must arrive in accordance with established characteristics. The importance of quality in production processes with proper procedures is vital for optimal organizational performance and for meeting customer needs. This article examines the use of Lean tools under a circularity approach to deliver defect-free products. Lean practices and tools play an important role within manufacturing industries to improve and enhance competitive advantage in the global marketplace. They also face increasing pressures to align their operations with sustainability goals. Production efficiency is expected to reach 71.70% and reverse logistics efficiency 50%, reducing downtime and availability. In summary, industry circularity improves operations with sustainable efficiency and benefits the economy and environment.

articleTitle: Systematic Review of the Impacts of Ship Emissions in Ports and Nearby Coastal Areas
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Shipping is a significant source of air pollution affecting air quality in ports and adjacent coastal areas. To understand this impact, it is essential to estimate atmospheric emissions. In this article, a systematic review of research that has estimated emissions of air pollutants such as SOx, NOx, and PM from ships in and around ports is conducted to assess their contribution to air quality. As a result, it is shown that ship emissions have a considerable impact on air quality. Among the pollutants studied, NOx is the most significant contributor, representing up to 60% of the pollutants (NOx, SOx and PM). Additionally, it is identified that the operational phase with the highest emission generation is the hoteling phase. It is also noted that container ships are the types of vessels that emit the highest amount of air pollutants.

articleTitle: An assessment of a ROS class using an educational mobile robot
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The Robot Operating System (ROS) is a middleware that standardizes robot programming, both in simulation and with real equipment. Despite this open-source tool being available for several years, there’s still a need to enhance its utilization in robotics education across all educational levels. In this study, a ROS class is assessed among university students using a commercial educational robot. The primary objective is to measure academic emotions in learning and student performance to determine the impact of the class using the open-access tool from a GitHub repository (https://github.com/joseVarelaAldas/ROS-Crowbot). This tool is based on the rosserial package, compatible with the ESP32 board. For class, CrowBot robots connected to the local wireless network via WiFi are used. TThe participants in this study were eight students from an electronics degree program at a higher education institution, who had no prior experience with ROS and received practical training using the educational mobile robot. For data collection on class performance, three parameters are assessed: execution time, functionality, and motivation, and to measure academic emotions, a validated self-report instrument is used. The results show an overall performance of 82.1%, and in the self-report on academic emotions, a high score in enjoyment (95%) and the lowest score in boredom (24.1 %) were obtained. In conclusion, the repository provides an interesting, practical, and accessible tool for an introduction into the world of robotics using ROS.

articleTitle: Novel Semi-active Upper-body Exoskeleton for Agriculture Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Exoskeletons with active joints arouse great interest for human power augmentation and assistive applications. In this article we present an innovative prototype of a portable shoulder and elbow exoskeleton, for assistance in agricultural tasks and heavy lifting in general. This exoskeleton provides controlled torque for the flexion/extension movements of shoulders and elbows and passive actuation of the movement of abduction and adduction of the shoulder. The remaining degrees of freedom of the shoulder system have been left unrestricted for comfort and little discrepancy with arm and shoulder movement. For this purpose, a serial mechanism has also been incorporated to facilitate scapular movement. On the other hand, the design incorporates a parallelogram beam mechanism to reduce the actuation torques and improve the controllability of the device. Moreover, the mechanical design of this mechanism was improved to ensure alignment between user elbow average flexion/extension rotation axis and that of the mechanism during the complete range of motion.

articleTitle: Methodological remarks of the design process of an App for risk management in an informal settlement
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Socially, economically and culturally excluded communities do not receive in the same way the benefits of information and communication technologies (ICT). This situation causes the digital divide to be amplified and reinforced. The contemporary challenge is to reverse this trend to seek an improvement in the quality of life, through the use and appropriation of digital technologies. This article presents the methodological remarks of the experience of designing an application, jointly between a public university and a marginalized community, to manage the risk of social conflict caused by limitations on access to drinking water in an informal settlement. The methodological proposal of the design process was conducted from the perspective of design justice and public university decolonization approach. This work contributes to the debate on the role of the public university in the process of computer technology production, aiming to contribute to the reduction of the digital divide effects and the improvement of the living conditions of vulnerable communities.

articleTitle: Linkage and innovation: the entrepreneur’s perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The results of an empirical study are presented, whose data were collected between October 2021 and May 2022, with the objective of identifying the relationship between the degree of linkage and innovation performance from the perspective of the company manager. The survey was sent through the Qualtrics technological platform; 150 companies with operations in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Spain, Panama, Puerto Rico and Venezuela participated. The hierarchical cluster analysis technique was used to group the companies according to the degree of linkage (defined as low, medium and high) with the university; after grouping the companies according to their degree of linkage, the statistical technique of Analysis of Variance was used to validate whether there was a statistically significant difference between groups for the level of innovation achieved (product, process and organizational). The analysis of variance tests (ANOVA) performed showed that there was no statistically significant difference in the degree of innovation achieved and the level of linkage for the sample studied. This result can be explained by the fact that the innovations carried out, as well as the level of interaction with the university, were reported for the period 2020 - 2021 during which the pandemic (Covid-19) affected and transformed the operations of both companies and universities, globally. Companies were forced to implement strategies and a whole series of adjustments in their activities to ensure their financial performance and survival.

articleTitle: Technical Feasibility of Photovoltaic Microgrids for Rural Communities in Panama
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: This study evaluates the technical feasibility of implementing photovoltaic microgrids in isolated rural communities in Panama, integrating solar generation and energy storage to provide a stable and continuous power supply. Using MATLAB/Simulink, the microgrid was simulated, focusing on the photovoltaic array, the boost converter, the DC-to-AC conversion, and an LC filter for signal conditioning. A droop control-based strategy was implemented to ensure power stability, and the effectiveness of battery storage was validated to maintain the supply during periods of low solar irradiation. The results demonstrate that the microgrid can operate autonomously and efficiently, meeting the electrical demands of the rural community. This study contributes to the advancement of sustainable energy solutions in Panama, aligning with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs 7 and 10). Future work will focus on real-world validation, control optimization, and the exploration of emerging technologies to enhance system resilience.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Solutions for Automatic Identification System (AIS) in Ships: Evaluation and Potential for Emissions Monitoring, a Review.
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The Automatic Identification System (AIS) is a critical tool for maritime safety, enabling ships to share essential information such as identification, position, course, and speed. While conventional AIS systems are effective, their high costs limit adoption among small-scale fishermen and operators of small vessels. This paper reviews recent developments in low-cost AIS solutions using technologies such as Software-Defined Radio (SDR) and microcomputers. The review highlights various studies that demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of these low-cost systems in maritime safety and environmental monitoring. Notably, these systems can estimate ship emissions, contributing to the reduction of marine pollution and improving sustainability in maritime transport. By examining the technological implementations, system designs, and methodologies, this paper aims to provide a comprehensive evaluation of the potential of low-cost AIS solutions in enhancing maritime safety and emission monitoring.

articleTitle: Demand Characterization for Interest Points of Solid Waste Management in Panama
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Effective waste management is critical for sustainable development, yet current information systems remain fragmented, making comprehensive and actionable data scarce. This study addresses the gap by developing integrated strategies to identify recycling entities and assess regional demands for recycling centers in Panama. Focusing on the provinces of Panama, Panama Oeste, Herrera, Los Santos, and Chiriquí, a detailed survey to capture insights into local recycling habits and needs is conducted.
