The findings are expected to guide decision-making for authorities and recycling entities, enhancing the efficiency of waste management initiatives and promoting public awareness and participation

articleTitle: Water quality analysis through the comparison of physicochemical parameters and the use of macroinvertebrates in the microbasin of La Zanguenga creek
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The study analyzed water quality by using physicochemical parameters and macroinvertebrates located in seven inter-basins of the La Zanguenga creek. The goal was to compare the effectiveness of each method. The monitoring took place over a 12-month period, where dry, transition and rainy seasons were considered. The results indicated that the water quality, as assessed through physicochemical parameters, reflected a moderate quality for the seven inter-basins of La Zanguenga Creek, with values ranging from 66.12 to 69.52. Conversely, the water quality, as assessed through the biological index (BMWP/PAN) presented very low values ranging from 8 to 21.8, signifying a polluted to very polluted state. These low biological index values can be attributed to environmental and anthropogenic disturbances in the study area. Overall, the results demonstrated that both methods complement each other, providing us with a more accurate and detailed analysis of the specific situation in the freshwater body, which has a positive impact on the environmental conditions required for each organism to thrive in a freshwater ecosystem.

articleTitle: Conceptual analysis of integrated watershed management in Río Indio for the natural environment and climate
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) in a basin requires the intervention of various disciplines and the active participation of citizens, decision-makers, and all key stakeholders in the watershed. This work proposes to use the conceptual maps methodology as a tool to visualize and understand the management of the Río Indio basin. Although this methodology has been widely applied in other countries, its use for watershed planning in Panama is still scarce. In 2022, González et al. [1] made a general approximation of Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) using conceptual maps for the Río Grande basin. For this work, the selection of the Río Indio basin is based on the impact it is expected to have as part of the solution to the water scarcity problem faced by the Panama Canal. This basin covers an area of 580 km², and its water resources are used mainly for agriculture, livestock, and human consumption. A problem and solution matrix was designed and applied, based on the Global Water Partnership (GWP) toolbox, to address the main issues within this watershed. Based on this matrix, conceptual maps for each discipline considered in IWRM were developed. These conceptual maps demonstrated the interconnections and relationships among the elements within each IWRM discipline. This simplified visualization facilitates understanding and applying the necessary measures for designing watershed management plans.

articleTitle: Proposal for the planning process for the automation of the design of panamanian crafts: Case of the Junco Hat (Cyperus holoschoenus)
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The agro-industry is defined as the economic activity developed in the territory, where the raw material in its production is of agricultural, livestock, aquaculture, or forestry origin. This activity can be either food-related or non-food-related and is processed in a way that aims to provide added value. In the context of this research proposal, we will contribute to the knowledge in non-food agro-industry, specifically the artisanal sector, with a focus on the junco hat. This project proposes a methodology structured in two stages, based on establishing a planning process for the automation in the creation of the mold used for crafting the junco hat, by using a new mold made with 3D technology. This approach aims to enhance the sustainability and productivity of non-food artisanal microenterprises in the agro-industrial sector, without altering the cultural value. This technology arises as an alternative in the face of global warming effects, where the “El Niño” phenomenon impacts the ecosystems of the junco and the trees used for crafting the wooden mold “cedro amargo”. 3D printing is characterized by customized manufacturing and the demand for parts made from various materials. This proposal is innovative and generates scientific knowledge. As a future line of research, sustainability management is proposed with the aim of rescuing and protecting nature and ecosystems for the conservation of the junco.

articleTitle: Impact of Preventive Maintenance on Productivity in a Textile Company: A Simulation Model in iThink
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Globalization has increased the demand for products, generating high competitiveness and significant production demands. In production processes, machinery breakdowns can affect planning and increase production costs. One way to prevent these breakdowns is through a preventive maintenance program. However, implementing these strategies requires time and money. In this context, simulation has become an extremely useful tool for analyzing production systems. This paper presents some future scenarios when implementing a preventive maintenance plan in a textile company. Using the iThink simulation software, the studied process was modeled, which allowed the establishment of future scenarios to understand how maintenance activities increase or decrease the productivity of the process.

articleTitle: Development of a Lightweight Kite-Balloon System for Atmospheric Observation
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Captive balloon systems capable of wind measurement for atmospheric turbulence studies typically require a large volume of lifting gas to carry heavy instruments, such as sonic anemometers, increasing equipment and operational costs. The availability of newer and lightweight sensors like the TriSonica Mini and a kite-balloon as a lifting platform led to the development of a lightweight and easy-to-manufacture package described in this paper. The package is designed to observe various atmospheric variables, including wind speed, temperature, humidity, and pressure. It incorporates an Attitude and Heading Reference System and a GNSS/GPS to compute the wind from the measured airflow from the sonic anemometer by accounting for body movements. Measurements are stored in a data logger and transmitted into the ground station with a telemetry module; additionally, ground station software is developed for live monitoring and alternative backup data storage. The supporting platform or gondola is designed to be lightweight, protect the sensors from environmental factors, and reduce pitching motion during operation. The paper compares wind measurements from the developed system with those from a ground-based sonic anemometer and presents preliminary results from field tests.

articleTitle: Increase inventory accuracy and availability through the implementation of a logistics process control model based on lean tools in SMEs in the retail sector
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: This scientific article aims to demonstrate the usefulness of the application of a novel inventory management model based on 3 tools: A control system for incoming and outgoing goods, a process monitoring system managed through a KANBAN canvas and a continuous improvement system based on a PHVA cycle to improve the logistics management of an SME in the retail sector. especially in the control of inventory accuracy and availability indicators. It was based on an initial diagnosis of the processes of the logistics area of the company under study, then appropriate inventory management policies were implemented, and the processes were re-engineered. The next step was to design a Dashboard to control the inflows and outflows of goods, which takes the information from the company’s ERP and allows it to anticipate omissions in the processes. Finally, staff were trained and a process monitoring system based on KANBAN and PDCA cycle was implemented. To monitor the key indicators, an inventory crossing process was designed, which compares the logical inventory level with the physical inventory once a week uninterruptedly, allowing inventory differences and the level of merchandise availability to be controlled. In conclusion, the implemented model has proven to be efficient in increasing the level of accuracy and availability of inventory, thus contributing to achieving significant savings for the company.

articleTitle: Analysis of the variation of the apparent radius of the Sun.
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Due to the dynamics of its surface, the Sun, our closest star, has been a constant subject of interest throughout the history of astronomy. Observing and analyzing this celestial body has been crucial for understanding not only variations in its apparent size and activity but also its evolution and influence on the solar system. Studying the Sun is essential for deepening our knowledge of its impact on the spatial and planetary environment. This research focuses on the evolution of the solar size from 1980 to 2020. To achieve this, information from the BASS2000 solar database was collected and analyzed, using data obtained from the spectroheliographs of the Meudon and Coimbra observatories. The analysis reveals an apparent solar radius with a peak near 685,000 km and a symmetric distribution. Although linear regression shows a possible upward trend in the Sun’s apparent radius, this should be interpreted with caution due to potential data variations and significant daily variability observed.

articleTitle: Exploring oxygen consumption of the bivalve Anadara tuberculosa under contrasting environmental conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Marine organisms must cope with environmental differences between the habitats they occupy through genetic, physiological and behavioral traits that allow them to adapt and survive across different spatial and temporal scales of climatic and oceanographic variation. Oxygen consumption of the bivalve mollusk Anadara tuberculosa was measured at two sites in the mangroves of Bahía de Chame (Pacific Panama), with contrasting pH and pCO2 levels. Oxygen consumption rates were recorded within the range of variability reported for other bivalve species (0.03 ± 0.02 mg/g/h). Small and random differences are reported between the marine-influenced site (0.02 - 0.04 mg/g/h) and the riverine-influenced site (0.01 - 0.06 mg/g/h). The observed variability appears to be a normal physiological response to the heterogeneous and highly variable environment of the estuaries and mangroves of Bahía de Chame.

articleTitle: Felicidad e Innovación: Una estrategia como impulsor de la producción científica.
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: La presente investigación describe los factores que influyen en el diseño de una estrategia que busca generar acciones y actividades que propendan por la felicidad organizacional como motor de la producción científica innovadora y de alta calidad. A través de una encuesta de veinticinco (25) preguntas aplicadas al equipo de profesionales de $\mathbf{I}+\mathbf{D}+\mathbf{i}$ de diversas facultades, se buscó identificar los aspectos clave que inciden en el bienestar subjetivo de los colaboradores colombianos y en su capacidad para generar conocimiento innovador y relevante en las diferentes áreas de formación. Los resultados sugieren que aspectos como la cultura organizacional, que promueve la autonomía, el reconocimiento y el trabajo en equipo, así como el bienestar subjetivo de los profesionales de $\mathbf{I}+\mathbf{D}+\mathbf{i}$, están estrechamente relacionados con la producción científica de alto impacto, siendo afectados por roles adicionales tales como administrativos, relación con empresas, académicos y extensión. La combinación de estas tareas genera preocupación en los profesionales de $\mathbf{I}+\mathbf{D}+\mathbf{i}$ dado que reduce su tiempo en el desarrollo de sus actividades de investigación, generando un impacto significativo y causando estrés laboral.

articleTitle: Process proposals for the automation of the manufacture of handicrafts: The case of the Sombrero de Junco
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Crafts are handmade creations that use traditional techniques and provide a tangible dimension to folklore, giving objects a cultural context and deep meaning. On the other hand, additive manufacturing encompasses a set of technologies that make it possible to create three-dimensional objects from a digital model. With this principle, additive manufacturing reduces manufacturing costs, speeds up manufacturing, and customizes products, among other advantages. In this sense, this work seeks to propose methodologies for the manufacture of Panamanian handicrafts, with a specific focus on the Sombrero de Junco, using 3D printing technology, without altering the authenticity and cultural value. To carry out these proposals, the research focuses specifically on the manufacture of the hat last, a collection of information with artisans of the Province of Los Santos and a literature review through Google Scholar is carried out. From this, 71 results were obtained, which were debugged and then reviewed. The research results in three proposals for the manufacture of the last, where they differ in the design process, as well as in the use of complementary tools, such as 3D scanners, cameras and the use of Artificial Intelligence Programs.

articleTitle: Análisis del impacto de un nuevo punto de acceso en la dinámica del tráfico urbano: estudio de caso del Campus VLS en Panamá
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Este estudio se enfoca en la evaluación del impacto de una nueva entrada vehicular desde la Av. Ricardo J. Alfaro hacia el Campus Víctor Levi Sasso (VLS) de la Universidad Tecnológica de Panamá (UTP) en la redistribución del flujo vehicular. Se utilizaron simulaciones en PTV VISSIM para modelar tanto las condiciones actuales como la infraestructura propuesta, analizando la movilidad y seguridad vial en el entorno. La metodología incluye la calibración y validación de modelos de tráfico, seguida de una evaluación comparativa de la situación actual frente a la propuesta de mejora. Los resultados muestran una reducción significativa en la congestión de la Vía Centenario durante el periodo vespertino, con una disminución de hasta un $\mathbf{1 6 . 1 \%}$ en el flujo vehicular en dirección A. Sin embargo, se observa un leve aumento de la congestión y una disminución en el nivel de servicio en la Av. Ricardo J. Alfaro. Además, se identifican reducciones notables en los tiempos de viaje hacia y desde el campus, con una disminución promedio del 43.9% en el tiempo de entrada y del $55.7 \%$ en el tiempo de salida durante el pico matutino. Este estudio destaca la efectividad de la reestructuración de la infraestructura vial sin aumentar la capacidad vial, ofreciendo mejoras sustanciales en la movilidad urbana y la eficiencia del tráfico en el área de estudio.

articleTitle: Design of a PID controller based on frequency techniques for temperature regulation
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a frequency-based PID controller for temperature regulation around an LM35 sensor from a fan. The objective is to develop a frequency-based PID controller using the Matlab and Matlab/Simulink platforms, and then, in conjunction with a lowcost Arduino microcontroller, validate its correct functionality. For this purpose, an algorithm was programmed to capture the temperature exerted by the fan at maximum power in the study area. Later, the system transfer function was obtained with this data using the Matlab “System Identification Toolbox” and, finally, the frequency-based PID controller was designed. As a result, a frequency-based PID controller was obtained that is capable of reacting quickly to disturbances and regulating the altered temperature around the LM35at room temperature.

articleTitle: Improvement of Milk Quality for Fresh Cheese Production through the DMAIC Methodology in the Company Agroindustria La Rochela Timbio, Cauca
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: This article reports on a study conducted at Agroindustria La Rochela to improve milk quality for fresh cheese production. The research aimed to identify causes of milk quality variability and propose improvements, particularly concerning pH levels, which impacted internal processes. The DMAIC (Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control) methodology was used, incorporating statistical and quality tools such as capability analysis, control charts, and cause-and-effect diagrams. In the Define phase, problems were identified, and a project team was established. The primary issue was the milk collection logistics, which led to pH levels below the acceptable limit. To resolve this, additional transportation was subcontracted, routes were reorganized using satellite maps, and new staff were trained. Consequently, collection time was significantly reduced, and the average milk pH improved to 6.60. This change increased the capability index (Cp) from 0.73 to 1.83, bringing the process closer to the 6 sigma level. Monitoring controls and records were put in place to track collection time and pH, ensuring proper oversight and necessary adjustments.

articleTitle: λ Paghe Basic Reproductive Number Invasion Analysis using a Three Compartment Epidemiological Model
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: This work investigates a three-compartment model for representing the epidemiological dynamics of temperate phages, using the $\lambda$ phage as a model organism. Temperate phages can switch between lysogenic and lytic pathways, providing differential survival advantages under varying environmental conditions. The model captures the dynamics of susceptible hosts, lysogenic infected hosts, and free viral particles (SLV). The study identifies critical limitations of the SLV model, such as the absence of an explicit lytic compartment. The study explores the conditions favoring lysogenic or lytic strategies through invasion analysis using the next-generation method theorem to estimate the R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. A critical carrying capacity is used to determine which strategy is advantageous under specific host densities. The findings emphasize the adaptability of temperate phages in switching between strategies based on environmental cues. The study concludes that more sophisticated models are needed to accurately represent the life-history traits of temperate phages, accounting for variable mortality rates, explicit lytic pathways, and the plasticity of temperate strategies. This research provides insights into the ecological and evolutionary contexts influencing the prevalence of temperate strategies in viral populations.

articleTitle: Evaluación de un modelo semidistribuido para la estimación del balance hídrico en la subcuenca del río Guararé
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: En Panamá, el acceso a agua y saneamiento juega un papel importante en el desarrollo de actividades cotidianas, así como para el crecimiento económico, calidad de vida y la salud de la población (Tejada, 2018). La subcuenca del río Guararé se localiza entre los ríos Tonosí y La Villa, cuenta con una superficie de 412 kilómetros cuadrados. Esta zona se destaca por sus actividades agrícolas y ganaderas predominantes; no obstante, se ha visto afectada por la deforestación y contaminación, estos factores han resultado en una considerable disminución de los niveles de caudal en el río (ANAM, 2007). Este estudio tiene como objetivo aplicar el modelo Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT) para estimar el balance hídrico en la subcuenca del río Guararé para el año hidrológico 2023.

articleTitle: Evolutionary Analysis of Sustainable Water Treatment in the City of Querétaro, Mexico
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Abstract-This study analyzes the evolution of water treatment practices in Santiago de Querétaro, Mexico, from 2013 to 2022, focusing on greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, energy consumption, financial costs, and contaminant reduction. Using methodologies from the IPCC and other sources, we estimated CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, and N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O emissions from local wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs). The findings indicate significant reductions in GHG emissions due to advanced treatment processes, with a $\mathbf{3 0 \%}$ decrease in CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions over the study period. Additionally, energy consumption was optimized through the implementation of more efficient technologies, resulting in a $25 \%$ reduction in overall energy use. Financial analysis revealed that despite initial higher costs, the long-term savings and environmental benefits justify the investment in sustainable technologies. Contaminant reduction was also substantial, with a $40 \%$ decrease in the concentration of harmful pollutants in treated water. The study underscores the importance of sustainable water treatment in mitigating climate change, enhancing public health, and improving environmental outcomes.

articleTitle: Evaluation of resilience in the Chiriqui Viejo River basin, Chiriqui, Panama in the context of climate change and extreme weather events.
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: This study examines the impact of climate change on the CHIRIQuí Viejo River basin, with a focus on the variability of precipitation patterns and their influence on the region’s flows. Using data collected from 1972 to 2001, climate variability was analyzed using the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI), a statistical method that quantifies anomalies in precipitation. The results indicate critical years in which the RLS reached extreme values, reflecting significant episodes of humidity and drought. For example, in 1972, the Cerro Punta station recorded an SPI of 3.5, denoting an exceptionally wet year, while in 1984, the Canas Gordas station experienced an SPI of ${- 1. 2 1}$, indicative of severe drought. The visual information provided by the heat maps clearly illustrates the spatial and temporal distribution of these events. Specifically, Figure 4 highlights how variations in altitude and geographic location within the basin directly affect precipitation patterns and, consequently, water management. The article highlights the critical need for water management policies that consider these patterns of climate variability to strengthen the resilience of local communities and ecosystems. In addition, the implementation of adaptation and mitigation strategies to respond to the adverse effects of climate change is suggested, based on a comprehensive approach that combines hydrological and climate models, vulnerability analysis, and case studies. In summary, this analysis provides a solid basis for future research and the development of more robust and adaptive policies, which are critical to ensure the sustainability of water resources in the Chiriquí Viejo River basin and other similar regions affected by climate change.

articleTitle: Influence of dilution factors on detection capability and accuracy of total reflection X-Ray fluorescence analysis of seawater samples
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Seawater analysis is crucial for monitoring marine ecosystem contamination, particularly that of heavy metals, which poses significant threats to marine life and human health. However, the matrix effect in seawater, caused by the presence of multiple compounds and interference, can lead to inaccurate results. Total reflection X-Ray Fluorescence (TXRF) is a highly sensitive technique for determining the elemental concentrations in samples; however, the high salt content in seawater can cause interference in the TXRF spectrum. This study aimed to evaluate the influence of dilution factors on the detection capability and accuracy of TXRF analysis of seawater. Surface seawater collected from Playa La Marinera, Tonosí, was filtered and diluted to $1: 5$, 1:10, and 1:20. Gallium was used as an internal standard, and the samples were analyzed using a S2 Picofox TXRF spectrometer. Statistical parameters, including detection limits, Poisson distribution, and deconvolution quality, were calculated for each sample to assess the optimal dilution. The results of this study will enhance the understanding of direct element measurements in liquids with high matrix content and contribute to the development of more accurate and reliable seawater analysis methods for monitoring marine ecosystem health.

articleTitle: Economic quantification of the impacts attributable to the accelerated rise in sea level due to climate change in the coastal marine zone of the Eastern Pacific of Panama
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The economic value of mangroves, calculated based on the products and services they provide, has been estimated by various authors. However, there is still no methodology that includes mangroves for the economic quantification of the financial impacts of mangroves. The economic value of mangroves, calculated based on the products and services they offer, has been estimated by various authors. However, there is still no methodology that includes mangroves for the economic quantification of the impacts attributable to accelerated sea level rise due to climate change, so the main objective of this study is to carry out this quantification using Geographic Information Systems (GIS) tools. From the results obtained, some 61 million balboas a year are being lost by not protecting the mangroves in the Eastern Pacific area alone, so it is clear that their conservation is of the utmost importance and that the activities to be developed in the coastal area must be adjusted to the natural characteristics of the site, seasonality, its adaptive capacity with the ecosystem and strategies for adaptation to climate change.

articleTitle: Electricity Public Service Quality Management in Colombia
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Electricity is essential for the economic and social development of communities. The national government in each territory regulates electricity because is a public service. Utilities manage the electricity supply to meet the communities’ demand while considering economic and financial feasibility. Regulation’s purpose is to ensure efficient, secure, and reliable operation within the sector, maintaining quality and safety. This paper contains an analysis of the management criteria for the quality of the electrical energy service and the indicators in the Caribbean region of Colombia.

articleTitle: Methodology to evaluate solar photovoltaic sources integration in an electrical grid
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The integration of Renewable Energies changes the one-way paradigm of operation in electrical grids imposing new challenges for grid operators to understand the effects of local generation and reverse flows. In this study, a methodology to evaluate the impact through the Hosting Capacity term has been developed and implemented in San Andres Island’s power grid. The methodology is used to evaluate voltage indicators, showing some variations that could imply the need to adjust protection schemes to maintain the operation of the network.

articleTitle: Phytosanitary Analysis of Trees in Summit Municipal Park
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: In recent decades, urban expansion in Central America and the Caribbean has led to significant landscape transformations, reducing green areas and the presence of trees threatening urban sustainability. Urban forests have a key role, providing ecosystem services such as temperature regulation and recreational areas; however, they face numerous challenges such as pollution and pests attacks. Summit Municipal Park, a key urban forest on the outskirts of Panama, hosts a high diversity of species whilst attracts more than 200,000 visitors annually. This may constitute a significant pressure on its phytosanitary status. The study evaluated 143 trees of 53 species in the park, revealing that 86% show signs of disease. The main conditions include dry branches (47.58%), termite damage (39.52%), and dead branches (31.45%). The most frequent species, such as Lagerstroemia speciosa with 16 individuals and Swietenia macrophylla with 20, also showed disease prevalence.

articleTitle: Petrographic, Chemical, and Morphological Characterization of Thermal Wells in the Valle de Antón Using Advanced Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The present work evaluates the petrographic, chemical, and morphological properties of rock samples from currently used thermal wells located in the Valle de Antón, Coclé Province. Through polarized light microscopy (PLM), subhedral clasts of white plagioclase (Plg) and quartz (Qz) in lower concentrations were identified, with the latter appearing as translucent, euhedral tabular crystals. Among the accessory minerals present, shows black point-like crystals that could be interpreted as inclusions of amphibole (Amp) or biotite. X-ray fluorescence analysis indicates that the rock sample contains 97.85% silica as the main component, 1.42% iron trioxide, and 0.43% aluminum trioxide. These minerals belong to groups associated with felsic rocks, which have a predominantly acidic chemical composition corresponding to the majority percentage of silicates. SEM images demonstrate the presence of microfissures and micropores, as well as biogenic siliceous microstructures corresponding to diatoms, indicating the aquatic depositional environment of the rock. The use of these techniques allows for a deeper characterization of the rock sample, including its petrological, chemical, and morphological properties, providing a solid framework for accurately understanding complex factors such as hydrothermal alteration and secondary recrystallization.

articleTitle: Efecto de métodos de secado sobre la calidad sensorial del café Geisha natural de Panamá
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: El secado es una etapa crucial en la producción de café de especialidad, ya que influye significativamente en las características organolépticas del producto final. Este estudio evaluó la calidad del café Geisha natural secado mediante cuatro métodos: camas africanas, liofilización, cuarto frío y secador inteligente. Se procesaron cerezas maduras de tres fincas de café de especialidad en Panamá, analizando las muestras en términos físicos y sensoriales. Aunque no se observaron diferencias estadísticamente significativas entre los métodos, el secado con camas africanas obtuvo la mayor puntuación promedio (90.25), mientras que el método de liofilización obtuvo la puntuación más baja (88.63). Los métodos de camas africanas y secador inteligente mostraron perfiles de sabor más complejos y típicos del Geisha, en contraste con la menor complejidad observada en el método de liofilización. Estos resultados sugieren que los métodos de secado pueden afectar de manera diversa la calidad del café Geisha, indicando la necesidad de más investigaciones que consideren variables adicionales como costos operativos y condiciones ambientales para determinar la viabilidad de cada método en términos de calidad y costo.

articleTitle: Sustainable Community Development and Learning Environments: A View from the Academy
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The world population is constantly increasing, mainly concentrating in large cities, while rural areas tend to empty out primarily due to a lack of opportunities. As is known, institutions of higher education not only must train the professionals a country needs, but they also must be committed to sustainable development and humanity to achieve a world with citizens co-responsible for human development. Therefore, this study has considered it relevant to focus on learning environments because it is necessary to improve people’s quality of life and to preserve and conserve our natural resources for future generations, based on the Design Thinking methodology as a collaborative work method that confronts and solves challenges or problems arising in a multidisciplinary organization and that must be addressed jointly to achieve effective and sustainable solutions. This study is framed in three types of learning environments: one linked with rural communities, another a community learning center connected with the elderly, and a community of students involved in the development of technological proposals requested by various regions of the country. These cases facilitate sustainable community development because organized communities are the ideal setting for social and economic transformations, becoming agents of change.

articleTitle: Use of Rayleigh Wave Velocity as a Parameter for Seismic Site Classification in Panama
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Site classification, based on the dynamic behavior of soils, is fundamental for the study of seismic hazard. The proposed methodologies emphasize two key parameters: the shear wave velocity of the soil and the site’s vibration frequency, for site classification. For estimating shear wave velocity, the analysis of surface waves is widely used through surface vibration signals to determine Rayleigh wave velocities. Modeling this response estimates the shear wave velocity profile, and the site is classified according to the average velocity. In comparison, a site classification based directly on Rayleigh wave velocities reduces computational cost and model complexity. Rayleigh wave velocities represent a parameter that can be measured without involving the modeling of soil strata. The Rayleigh wave velocity depends on the dynamic properties of the soil from the surface to a certain depth and includes the overall behavior of the surface stratigraphy, making it directly useful for site characterization. Additionally, because the vibration frequency is a function of soil stiffness, Rayleigh wave velocity can be used to estimate the site’s vibration frequency. This study presents a site classification methodology based on the application of Rayleigh wave velocities as the primary parameter, as an alternative classification approach aligned with conventional methodologies based on shear wave velocity and site classification methodologies based on site vibration frequency. Its application in the field and at points of interest in Panama achieved results similar to those obtained through conventional methodologies with an absolute average margin of error of 6%.

articleTitle: Sustainable improvement in a textile company by applying the Lean Green Manufacturing model
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The textile industry is a significant player in manufacturing, contributing significantly to the economy. However, one of its considerable challenges is delivery delay, which calls for more efficient and sustainable processes. To address this issue, the proposed solution aims to improve the supply chain, reduce idle time and optimize waste management, with the goal of improving the company’s research processes. The Lean-Green tool is the chosen approach, as it offers a targeted reduction of environmental impact, improves sustainable processes, and increases customer satisfaction. Implementing this approach requires a considerable improvement of at least 15%. The tool promises to optimize processes, leading to ongoing increases in efficiency, which is a comprehensive and long-lasting strategy for enhancing textile production. The Arena program was used to validate and optimize improvement processes in the company, resulting in increased productivity.

articleTitle: Experiences and actions on Environmental Education in Solid Waste Management in Panama
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Through a review of actors, programs, projects and publications of experiences in environmental education and solid waste, financed by SENACYT, the descriptive study presented here was carried out. The objective of this study was to identify the scope of various experiences in environmental education and solid waste carried out by academia, public institutions, and non-governmental organizations. The methodology used was the application of a multiple-choice questionnaire. The results allow us to identify the main focus of the various programs at the methodological level as ‘learning by doing‘. At the national level, important steps have been taken to establish environmental education and recycling experiences, but the development of an environmental education policy and a curriculum that allows educators, public institutions, and NGOs to manage the complexity and multifaceted nature of solid waste management is still pending.

articleTitle: Obstacle avoidance and local path planning based on reinforcement learning for hexacopter drone in simulated environments
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: This article details the development, training, and application of an artificial intelligence (AI) agent designed for autonomous navigation tasks in a hexacopter drone. The focus is on two key subtasks: obstacle avoidance and local path planning. Using the Gazebo physics simulator, a simulated environment based on an oil palm plantation was created. The drone, controlled by an LQG controller for flight and trajectory management, was integrated with an AI agent trained using the D3QN (Dueling Double Deep Q-Network) reinforcement learning algorithm. This setup allowed the drone to autonomously determine destination coordinates and navigate safely through the environment using LIDAR sensors for real-time obstacle detection. The results demonstrate that the D3QN agent effectively reaches target positions while avoiding obstacles, showcasing the efficacy of reinforcement learning in training local path planners for drones in complex scenarios. These findings underline the potential of using simulation-based reinforcement learning for enhancing drone navigation and operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Ocean Energy Potential in Panama: An Assessment for Sustainable Energy Development
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: This research aims to evaluate the potential of ocean energy in Panama as an alternative for clean and sustainable electricity production through predictive and comparative analysis, considering the descriptive variables of each alternative concerning the oceanic conditions of Panama. This analysis focuses on wave energy, tidal energy, osmotic energy or salinity gradient energy, ocean thermal energy, and ocean current energy. First, the potential of each alternative was evaluated concerning Panama’s oceanic conditions. Then, the alternatives with the greatest potential were identified. As a result of this research, the energy potential of the five alternatives was categorized into high, moderate, and low, with ocean thermal energy and wave energy showing high energy potential. Subsequently, tidal energy and marine current energy showed moderate potential. Finally, osmotic energy or salinity gradient energy projected low potential due to the limited availability of freshwater bodies flowing into the seas. Additionally, it was justified that the development of technologies associated with these energy alternatives is experiencing significant and accelerated advancements that would benefit their implementation in Panama. This could significantly contribute to the diversification of the energy matrix in a sustainable manner, thus reducing dependence on fossil sources and minimizing environmental impact.

articleTitle: Characterization of the atmospheric boundary layer over a tropical arid area using an airborne sonic anemometer and fixed wing UAV
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Measurements within the atmospheric boundary layer are key to obtaining better understanding of the air-surface interactions and to improve models. One way to conduct this is by using uncrewed aerial vehicles with sonic anemometers, inertial navigation systems, and other instruments. This technique is explored by using an in-house experimental fixedwing UAV, with a miniature sonic anemometer, in a flat arid area found in the Sarigua National Park. Vertical profiles of wind velocity and sonic temperature were compared to ground station data and a wind profile model based on the BusingerDyer relations. The aircraft system’s averaged wind data agreed with the modeled wind profile at low altitudes, within the surface layer. However, a departure from the model was found at greater altitudes. Wind direction measured with the airborne system remained close to those measured with the ground station. Simultaneously, profiles of sonic temperature were obtained, registering a decrease with altitude during the afternoon measurements, while a morning sounding had a different shape.

articleTitle: Stress and Surface Fluid Contact Angle Analysis on Ultrananocrystalline Diamond (UNCD) Films grown by Hot Filament Chemical Vapor Deposition (HFCVD)
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The research described in this article focused on investigating the influence of three gas mixtures on the growth of ultrananocrystalline diamond (UNCD) films, using hot filament chemical vapor deposition (HFCVD). The focus was on residual stress analysis and measurement of fluid drop contact angle on UNCD films’ surfaces. Three films were grown using different flow rates of hydrogen (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>), methane (CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>), and argon (Ar) gas mixtures. The chemical, structural, and residual stress properties of the UNCD films were characterized using Raman and X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopies (XPS), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), respectively. The hydrophilicity and hydrophobicity of the surfaces were evaluated through water drop contact angle measurements. The results show that the gas mixture has a significant impact on the residual stress and wettability properties of the UNCD films. In particular, the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> flow rate and the addition of Ar gas flow influence the formation of more homogeneous surfaces and the variation of residual stress, which is crucial for applications to microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) and other advanced UNCD film-based technologies.

articleTitle: Analysis and Detection of Hate Speech: A Comparative Study of NLP Transformer Models
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Every minute millions of comments are posted about a certain context. People are becoming more and more involved with the wide spread of social media. It is so easy to post almost anything on social media, given the amount of unregulated content, which has given way to a proliferation of aggressive and harmful content commonly called hate speech on the Internet. One of the most important challenges in the area of Natural Language Processing (NLP) is the detection of semantic analysis in texts. We propose to design and develop a model for the automated detection of hate speech on social networks. A case study was carried out using a dataset extracted and labeled by us to evaluate the model, achieving excellent results.

articleTitle: Enhancing Agricultural Efficiency and Sustainability in Panama: Solar Drying with Phase Change Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive review of the advancements in solar dryers and the application of phase change materials (PCMs) in the agricultural drying process. It examines various solar drying technologies, including direct, indirect, hybrid, and tunnel dryers, and underscores significant experimental studies and technological developments in each category. The review also explores various strategies for enhancing the performance of solar dryers, such as integrating heat exchangers and implementing advanced control systems. Special emphasis is placed on the role of PCMs in optimizing the drying process, analyzing their properties, energy efficiency benefits, and impact on the quality of the final product. By synthesizing the latest research, this paper provides valuable insights into the potential of solar dryers and PCMs to improve sustainability and efficiency in agricultural drying practices.

articleTitle: Assessment of natural radiation in a former uranium mine: A technical capacity building development
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The utilization of tracers is essential for understanding the behavior, transportation routes, final destinations, and deposition of sediments. In hydrogeological investigations, nuclear techniques employ radioactive isotopes as artificial tracers. However, the implementation of nuclear technologies demands caution, and there is a scarcity of publications addressing the environmental and human impact of radioactive tracers. The research project “Development of Radiometric Methods and Modelling for Sediment Transport Measurement in Coastal Systems and Rivers,” coordinated by the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) and conducted by the Centro de Desenvolvimento da Tecnologia Nuclear (CDTN), proposes an approach based on natural radiation. The Caldas Decommissioning Unit (UDC Caldas) was selected for this study owing to its decommissioning requirements and high levels of natural radiation. One of the research objectives is the transfer of technology and knowledge, as evidenced by the collaboration with the Universidad Tecnológica de Panamá (UTP). Researchers conducted surveys to acquire georeferenced data on naturally occurring radionuclides, that is, potassium (<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">40</sup>K), thorium (<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">232</sup>Th), and uranium (<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">238</sup>U), using a portable spectrometer at UDC Caldas. Subsequently, the data processing was carried out using the ‘R’ programming language and QGIS software to generate maps for examining the measured variables in classes (natural breaks) and interpolation (Inverse Distance Weighting - IDW).

articleTitle: Towards Sustainability and Resilience of Buildings Against Structural Deterioration in Tropical Climates
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Accelerated urban growth demands sustainable construction and maintenance practices, particularly for existing structures. This research examines the impact of tropical climates on building performance and explores strategies to enhance the resilience and behavior of these systems. A field survey analyzed 91 structures in Panama, a country with a tropical climate. The data explored the prevalence of various pathologies affecting these buildings, focusing on those related to climate exposure. Additionally, case studies examined the influence of architectural design, material compatibility, and construction details on building performance. The study revealed that tropical climate significantly impacts the structural resilience of buildings. Moisture-related issues were the most common pathology, affecting over half of the structures. Most of the buildings in the sample had concrete masonry walls and concrete slab roofs. The analysis identified critical factors influencing building deterioration, including architectural design choices, material compatibility issues, and deficiencies in construction details. This research highlights the critical need for resilient buildings in local climates. It shows how tropical climates significantly affect building performance and underscores the importance of climate-responsive design, material selection, construction practices, and maintenance. By implementing these strategies, we can adapt maintenance and construction practices to create sustainable and resilient buildings capable of withstanding the challenges of tropical climates. This approach not only improves building performance and longevity but also ensures long-term sustainability.

articleTitle: Solutions for net-zero energy-oriented renovation of buildings: Case of a low apartment building in tropical climate
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: The project seeks to convert apartment buildings in Panama into net-zero energy buildings, taking advantage of the potential for energy savings and emissions reductions in the region. The study includes collecting similar developments, defining a typical building according to Panamanian regulations, and surveying Panama City to obtain design data. DesignBuilder with EnergyPlus software simulates a four-story building, identifying energy efficiency measures for the tropical climate and estimating savings and thermal comfort. The simulations are divided into three phases: consumption and comfort evaluation, analysis of important design variables, and multi-objective optimization. The first phase evaluates energy consumption and comfort in the most occupied areas of the building. The second phase identifies significant design variables, such as glass type and exterior wall material. The third phase looks for technically and economically feasible solutions, highlighting clay brick walls. Multi-objective optimization analysis was performed with plots, pivot tables, and a multivariate analysis in orange software. Solutions for tropical climates are essential for environmental sustainability, energy efficiency, adaptation to climate change, and fostering innovation and economic development.

articleTitle: Tumor detection and diagnosis with transformer-based artificial intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: In Panama, malignant tumors are one of the leading causes of death, accounting for $16.3 \%$ of deaths in 2016, a decrease of $1.8 \%$ compared to 2012. However, between 2012 and 2022, the total reduction was only $3.1 \%$. This slow progress underscores the need for improved diagnostic and detection systems. With this project, a tumor diagnosis and detection system based on artificial intelligence was developed to reduce diagnosis time, increase accuracy and support specialists, addressing the high demand. Deep learning models and a dataset of labeled medical images were used. The system will combine image processing techniques and artificial intelligence algorithms to identify and diagnose tumors. The models developed in this project achieved great efficiency in time and accuracy by processing large amounts of data, which is very beneficial to reduce the demand for the early detection of benign and malignant tumors, specifically the models provide the area where the tumor is located and a brief diagnosis that determines tumor characteristics

articleTitle: Dynamic Modeling of a 3 Degree of Freedom Helibot: Integration of LQG and PI Controllers for Precise Trajectory Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: This article extensively explores the dynamics of the Helibot 3DOF system, a commonplace in control labs, employing the Lagrangian formulation. It addresses a research gap by offering a detailed dynamic derivation, encompassing the transformation of positions, velocities, and inertia matrices between rotating and fixed frames. Utilizing an operational Helibot and a CAD model, a linearized state-space model is derived. A controller, integrating PI and LQG strategies, is developed, and its performance is assessed through simulations, considering criteria such as settling time and noise resistance. This work enhances the comprehension of the dynamics and control of the Helibot, highlighting the efficacy of the Lagrange formalism implemented in software with symbolic derivation. This method proves efficient in analyzing the kinematics and kinetics of interconnected bodies, contributing to the overall understanding of the system’s behavior.

articleTitle: Study of water resource management in the Juan Díaz basin through the generation of conceptual maps
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: River basins are influenced by various factors, which is why Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) is essential. IWRM may be new in Panama because this type of study has not been carried out in many of the country’s basins. But it is a great tool for decision-making in other countries. The Juan Díaz River basin was chosen for this research because it is a well-known basin with a high population density with 2856.7 inhabitants/ $\mathrm{k m}^{2}$ in the lower basin, considering that in other river basins in the country, such as the $\mathrm{N}^{\circ} 132$ (Santa María River) has a density of 13.15 inhabitants/$\mathrm{k m}^{2}$. In that sense, a great portion of Panama’s city population will be linked and affected positive or negatively. Basin problems and solutions were analyzed using the Global Water Partnership (GWP) toolbox. The GWP Toolbox presents information using conceptual maps and it is based on available references. Conceptual maps allow for summarizing all the information collected and interconnecting ideas, thus making it easier for decision-makers and the population, in general, to understand and take integrated actions for the well-being of the basin. In the present study, through the construction of conceptual maps, the different problems that the basin presents and the solutions to them are shown, how these situations, despite being shown from different disciplines, are interconnected with each other.

articleTitle: Assessment of the current state of Chiriquí River Basin, Panama: Environmental, economic, and policy perspectives for sustainable water resource management
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Río Chiriquí Viejo Watershed (Basin No. 108) in Chiriquí, Panama, represents a crucial ecological and socioeconomic region facing many challenges, including environmental degradation, social issues, economic pressures, and infrastructure shortcomings. This study aims to thoroughly assess the basin’s current condition, focusing on its natural and climatic aspects, primary water uses, economic activities, and existing policies and regulations. This research enhances the analysis and synthesis of diverse information by utilizing the Global Water Partnership’s Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) Toolbox and conceptual maps. The basin’s varied climate and topography support rich biodiversity and an extensive river network. Nonetheless, agricultural activities have significantly transformed the landscape, reducing forest cover and increasing soil erosion, degrading water quality, and posing significant challenges for sustainable management. Furthermore, while hydroelectric facilities are a crucial renewable energy source, they also disrupt natural water flow, leading to environmental issues. This study combines environmental, economic, and policy perspectives to guide sustainable water resource management strategies in Basin No. 108.

articleTitle: Stiffness Impact on the Design and Sustainable Functioning of Vortex Bladeless Turbines
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Stiffness in a bladeless wind turbine is crucial for determining the system’s natural frequency, oscillation amplitude, and efficiency in converting mechanical wind energy and dissipating it. Material selection is essential for an optimal Bladeless Vortex design. The material’s stiffness and damping ensure efficient, sustainable, and durable operation, maximizing wind energy conversion and affecting the turbine’s lifespan and maintenance. This study used dynamic simulations in Python to analyze the design, operation, and behavior of a Vortex Bladeless turbine made from E-Glass Fiber, Carbon Fiber, and Epoxy Carbon UD 230 GPa. Their stiffnesses were considered for performance impact. Variables influencing the vorticity phenomenon, including natural frequency, system displacement, interacting forces, air speeds, and power production, were analyzed. Mathematical expressions describing the phenomenon were developed and implemented in a Python program within the Spyder environment, incorporating input variables, displacement, and power graphs for the three materials. The simulations provided a comprehensive analysis of how each material affects turbine efficiency and power output. Results showed that E-Glass Fiber is the best material for sustainable Vortex Bladeless turbine operation, producing 6.12 mW. Carbon Fiber generated 4.08 mW, and Epoxy Carbon UD 230 GPa produced 2.04 mW. This finding supports using E-Glass Fiber for optimal performance, offering a balance of efficiency, cost, and material properties, and underscores the importance of material science in renewable energy technology.

articleTitle: Portable Decontamination System based on Cold Atmospheric Plasma and UV-C Light
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: This paper presents the design and testing of a portable decontamination system based on cold atmospheric plasma and UV-C light that could serve to decontaminate medical devices in remote areas or during epidemiological crises and natural disasters, as well as other items whose material composition makes them unsuitable for traditional decontamination methods used in hospitals. The efficacy of the prototype was verified through biological testing using bacteria Escherichia coli and Bacillus subtilis, as well as microorganisms commonly found in people’s hands. Results show that with a short exposure time of 5 minutes there was a log reduction of 1.91 for Escherichia coli and larger than 6 for Bacillus subtilis, meaning a disinfectant effectiveness of $98.8 \%$ and $100 \%$, respectively. Furthermore, two DBD reactors were used in asynchronous operation-mode to reduce energy consumption without sacrificing the species generated and the ionic wind produced.

articleTitle: Evaluation of coastal vulnerability for Parita’s Bay coastline
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Coastal Vulnerability Index (CVI) was developed for Guayaberos’ and Monagre’s beaches, located within the Parita’s Bay coastline. CVI included seven variables: coastal elevation, coastal slope, geomorphology, inundation, tidal amplitude, wave height, and land use. Geographic Information System (GIS) tools were used to define highly vulnerable sites. Results showed that high vulnerability was mostly linked to geomorphology, land use, and elevation. Meanwhile, coastal slope indicated varied vulnerability. Inundation, mean tidal amplitude, and wave height were linked to low vulnerability. Overall CVI ranged from 4.28 to 11.29, with a mean of 7.67 and median of 7.14 for both beaches. Approximately $52 \%, 26 \%, 15 \%$, and $6 \%$ of the coastline was classified into moderate, high, low, and very high vulnerability categories, respectively. These findings underscore the need for targeted conservation efforts in Parita’s Bay, particularly in ecologically significant areas, and for coastal planning.

articleTitle: Challenges and opportunities for sustainable agriculture in terms of pesticides: a case study in Tonosí
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Pesticides are essential for increasing crop yields and ensuring food security. However, their use poses significant environmental and health challenges. This study discusses the challenges to and opportunities for sustainable agriculture through the analysis of an inventory of pesticides marketed in the district of Tonosí, in the province of Los Santos, Republic of Panama. It was observed that there are many pesticides that are allowed in Panama but have been banned in many other countries due to their health and environmental impacts. To achieve sustainability, it is essential to integrate practices such as Integrated Pest Management (IPM), biopesticides, and precision agriculture, along with education and regulatory support. Balancing the benefits of pesticides with the need for environmental conservation and the protection of human health is key to a sustainable agricultural future.

articleTitle: Biocarbon Synthesis Methods for Anode Electrodes: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: This review analyzes hard carbon and its derivatives for energy storage applications, specifically as electrodes and anodes in batteries and supercapacitors. Various types of hard carbon have demonstrated significant improvements in terms of storage capacity and cycle stability. The benefits of using biomass by-products, such as agricultural, forestry, and organic waste, are highlighted, particularly when comparing conversion capacities, porosity, and performance. This review details types of biomass conversions, focusing on pyrolysis and chemical activation. It concludes that biocarbon and hard carbon are both viable and promising, positioning them as essential technologies for developing sustainable and efficient energy storage systems.

articleTitle: Supply Chain Disruption After Collapse of Bridge at the Port of Baltimore
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: Early in the morning of March 26, the containership Dali carrying nearly 4,700 shipping containers attempted to depart from the Port of Baltimore. Its destination was Sri Lanka. While navigating on the navigation channel of the Port of Baltimore, the containership lost power and control of the steering system and ended up colliding with one of the piers of the Francis Scott Key bridge causing the bridge to collapse. Several construction workers died as a result of the accident and the traffic to enter and leave the harbor of the Port of Baltimore was blocked for weeks. The collapse of the Francis Scott Key bridge impacted not only the US economy but also global supply chains. Cargo owners, end customers, logistics companies, shipping lines and entire communities were affected at some degree. In this paper, the disruption in global supply chains caused by the collapse of the Francis Scott Key bridge is discussed and the role of technology, specifically intelligent supply chain control towers, to respond rapidly and cost-effectively to unexpected events that disrupt supply chains, is also discussed.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization of Small Centrifugal Pumps for Liquid Hydrogen Transport Applications Using CFD Tools
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)

authors.preferredName: José M. Sánchez De La Hoz

abstract: Due to the climate change effects and high fossil fuel consumption to supply the global energy demand, scientific studies have been conducted to reduce the pollutant emissions and improve the energy generation processes. In this sense, cryogenic flow transport processes for hydrogen and electrical energy generation have promoted the application of alternative fuels under complex working conditions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. With the aim to analyze and optimize the application of mechanical devices for liquid hydrogen transport processes, this research proposes a predictive analysis of a cryogenic pumps based on numerical simulations with CFD tools in a virtual environment. To achieve accurate results, turbulence models are applied to study and predict the liquid hydrogen behavior and its interaction with impeller blades of centrifugal pumps. In consideration with the complex analysis of turbulent and cryogenic flows, a CFD tool is computed to solve and describe the workflow behavior around the blades under different working conditions. Finally, a multi-objective optimization method based on CFD simulations is proposed to improve the impeller design of the small centrifugal pump and reduce costs with computational tools.

articleTitle: Experimental Assessment of Reused PET Geogrids for Reinforcement of Unpaved Rural Roads
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Engineering, Sciences and Technology Conference (IESTEC)
abstract: New methods to reuse waste have become a priority due to the accumulation of plastic waste. In Panama, a sparse 5% of plastic waste is recycled, indicating that there is a large amount which is deposited in sanitary landfills. Unpaved roads are frequently used in rural regions of Panama, where the volume of traffic does not justify the investment of a paved road or street. However, it is important to mention that these rural roads are of vital importance for the transport of agro-industrial products, as well as the transit of tractors and machinery. The objective of this research is to evaluate the behavior of plastic waste used as raw material to create a geogrid prototype that can be installed in unpaved roads, improving their performance. The determination of its effectiveness will be analyzed by subjecting plastic waste to mechanical tests in accordance with applicable international standards, which include the characterization of polyethylene terephthalate (PET). Results from this research show that the tensile resistance of PET strips is somewhat in range with lowperformance geogrids, however plate load testing seems to indicate that inclusion of these elements compromises the performance of an unpaved road section.
